a box owns the border it strokes inside itself, and the ink gate that reports otherwise moves into the framework -- where two of three screens discovered they had never asked it. Filed catalog and the axis re-judged 97 -> 98 as the push gate demanded, the point going to the disabled cascade R1668/R1669 closed rather than to this round's own work. THE RULE: `containment::escapes` compared a mark against its owner's BOX, and a border is ink the box owns inside that box, so a child painted at the owner's full width covered the outline and was reported contained -- CSS has had border box versus content box from the beginning and nothing here expressed the second. R1671 pinned that as a test asserting the WRONG answer with a note saying to rewrite it on the round that fixed it; this is that round. The inset is a match over every `BorderPlacement` rather than a test for one of them, because the first draft asked `is it Inside` and returned the box otherwise, which is right for Outside and WRONG for Center: a centred stroke straddles the edge, so half its width is inside the box and a partially covered pixel is covered, so the inside half rounds up. AND THE PLACEMENT HALF IS PUBLIC, because a caller computing the inset itself is a second copy of the rule free to disagree with the check that reports it. ABSOLUTE PLACEMENT IGNORES PADDING, which is the measurement that made the widget repair a different repair from the one it looked like: the first pass gave `config_form`'s controls a padding equal to their own frame, re-measured, and found the two stepper buttons of every integer row STILL standing on the outline -- the padding had moved the value text and nothing else, because the steppers are placed at PUBLISHED part rectangles and an absolutely-placed child is positioned against its parent's border box. So `lay_parts` lays a shape's affordances in the control's CONTENT rectangle, `control_frame(shape)` says how much that is (two of six shapes put their parts inside a container that strokes `control_skin`), `CONTROL_FRAME` is the width `control_skin` builds its border FROM so the declaration and the paint are one number by construction, and the correspondence is asserted over EVERY arm by reading the border width back out of the painted scene -- a judgement about what a painter does goes wrong silently, and a shape that gained a skin would start painting its own parts over its outline with every test green. In the crate, so every consumer followed. The screen-A allowance that named the two remaining owners is DELETED: an exception mechanism holding the empty set is a place for the next escape to be filed instead of fixed. *** THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED. Screen B holds a byte-identical copy of the ink metric and never called the check with it, and screen C had neither -- so putting screen B's three scrolling panes back over the outlines of the panels holding them was caught by NOTHING, while the same break on screen A was caught immediately. Three mechanical copies of one rule is the immediate-lift case, and the hazard was never the duplication: it was that a metric a screen owns but does not use is a vocabulary the screen cannot speak. `pinion_core::test_fixtures::screen_ink` is that vocabulary -- the stand-in (width font-independent and conservative, height the laid-out line box, because deciding the vertical against a constant makes the gate a fact about the host's fonts), the off-window split, the assertion -- with four negative controls of its own, and all three screens ask. WHAT THE TWO NEW ASKERS FOUND, none of it visible to anything they already ran: screen B's three panes over their panels' outlines, repaired blind by the previous pass and now behind a gate that would have reported them; and on screen C five classes of defect in five different swept states, reported one state at a time because the gate stops at the first -- 32 marks as it opens, then 13, then 9 with a card selected, then 1 with the preset menu open, then 25 with every card shrunk to one cell. Every run placed at an exact rectangle had NO overflow policy, so a label longer than its fixed box was painted past it rather than shortened -- 32 marks including four of the app bar's own, on the one screen of three that never set what screens A and B set on every run. A code chip's word box was wider than the chip at two sites, each from a separately picked inset, which is one rule written twice and got wrong twice. A card reserved only its RESTING outline, so the moment it became the selected one and swapped its 1px outline for the 2px ring, its header and every row of its body stood on the ring's second pixel; the reservation is derived from the two widths now and is deliberately CONSTANT rather than a function of selection, because a content rectangle that changed with the ring would move every row when a person selects a card. And a header too narrow for its own chrome computed a title width with `.max(40)` on the end and measured everything after it from that clamped number, so a card shrunk to one board cell painted `LIVE` 65px past its own frame -- R1668's shape, one fact with two clamps. It gives way in a STATED order now (identity, then the affordance strip dropping from the left so the last-declared stays nearest the edge a hand reaches for, then the ready badge, then the title) and a part that does not fit is not painted; the sweep asserts BOTH sides of that branch, since a give-way that never happens and one that never stops are both invisible to a one-sided check. THE PRESET MENU IS A POPUP, not a child of the bar that opens it: it hung 81px below its parent, which is an escape and is also what a drop-down is -- anchored, not bounded, which is why the reference toolkit at 6.11 makes a menu a top-level popup. Moving it is not checkable by itself and that is the trap: the paint and the hit test both read `preset_item_rect`, so changing that function moves BOTH and no assertion comparing them can notice. The shape is pinned against something that is not itself -- the chip: the first row hangs under it, the panel lines up with it, and the menu stays inside the window. THE COUNTERFACTUAL DRIVER HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, found by trying to use it: `--manifest-path` was not known to consume its value, so `cargo test --manifest-path examples/<x>/Cargo.toml` -- which in this repo IS a screen's whole suite, every example being its own package -- was refused as a test-name filter. A screen's gate therefore could not be a counterfactual gate at all, which is where three of this round's breaks are visible. `VALUE_FLAGS` plus two cases in the driver's own tests. 15/15 counterfactuals caught (5 crate, 2 screen A, 1 screen B, 7 screen C) after CF-8 was the finding; two were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing. The two ink ratchets were regenerated by their producer under the font pin, which is the whole 224-surface census -- a partial run is refused, correctly.

the ink backlog R1672's rule surfaced is paid off -- 56 marks across seven surfaces, all one class -- and the three defects the repair then found underneath them. Filed catalog: two catalogue widgets gained a derivation they did not have (the checkbox's tick is now a RELATION to the square that holds it; the group box's title band is the tallest thing in it), and the group box gained the first self-containment test a bordered painter in this crate has ever had. THE LIFT IS THE FIRST MOVE AND ITS COUNT IS THE ARGUMENT: `containment::content_of(rect, Option<&Border>)` is the arithmetic half of `content_rect`, for the side that is PLACING children and so has the border before it has the node. Three screens had written the same `const fn panel_content` by hand with the inset spelled `1`, and the re-measurement found seven more surfaces owing the same repair; a rule with ten independent implementations is ten chances for one to disagree with the check that reports it, and here that check IS the other half. THE 56 WERE ONE THING, measured per surface rather than assumed: a child laid at its owner's BOX where the owner strokes a border inside it. property grid 29 (every row), node editor 10 (four header strips, six ports), input chip 10, graph diff 6, plus the data grid, the group box and the inspector. Seven repairs, each derived: the grids and the group box RESERVE their frame as padding -- the instrument that works for a FLOW child and deliberately not the one R1672 needed for published part rectangles, where an absolutely-placed child ignores its parent's padding; the node editor names its two border widths and reserves the WIDER constantly so a card's header and every port keep their place when it is selected (screen C's shape, arrived at again); the inspector does the same for its cursor ring; the graph-diff node's name is placed by the FLOW inside that reservation, having been authored as a rect in WINDOW coordinates on a text node whose container is already absolutely placed. ★THE INPUT CHIP'S PADDING WAS TRANSPOSED and its own comment had said so for rounds: `with_padding` takes `(left, top, right, bottom)` and the call passed `(0, PAD, 0, PAD)` under a comment reading `horizontal padding` -- twelve pixels above and below the label and NONE beside it. The containment rule turned a stale comment into a failing measurement. ★THE VIRTUAL TABLE'S LOAD BAR was shrinking under its own fill: the track and the fill are absolutely placed at one origin so they overlay, and an absolutely-placed child does not shrink with its parent, so when the flex pass narrowed the cell the fill kept the width it was sized from. The deficit goes to the label beside it (R1656's rule applied where it was written to be applied), so no number in that function has to be right. ★★THE CHECK MARK IS A RELATION, NOT A TOKEN. `box_size` and `glyph_size_px` are two independent numbers deciding one thing between them, so three consumers put a 16-18px tick in a 14-16px square where its shaped ink is 20-22 tall. The face is derived now -- the declared size, or the largest whose LINE BOX the square's CONTENT holds, a ceiling so a generous square keeps what it asked for. Two findings came out of writing it: the first draft INVERTED `line_box` by hand and the sweep caught it on its first run (at three pixels of content the algebra said nothing fits while a 1px face's line box is exactly three), so the answer steps down against the function instead of solving a copy of it; and a square with no room for any tick answers NONE rather than a one-pixel mark on its own outline, the arm the sweep also insists on reaching. ★★★THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS AGAIN A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED, TWICE: with the group box repaired, removing its frame reservation AND removing its title band's knowledge of the checkbox it holds both left this crate's whole suite GREEN. `pinion-widget-paint` had no test that a bordered painter's content stays inside its own frame, so only a CONSUMER booting could see it, one screen at a time -- the shape R1655 recorded for this same crate. The repair is that test, written against the framework's own `test_fixtures::screen_ink::assert_contained_ink`, the one three screens run, so a widget and the screens holding it are judged by one rule. AND IT FOUND A THIRD DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, in the arm with no checkbox at all: the LEGEND overflowed the band by two pixels. Three tokens decided that height between them and nobody had compared any pair; it is the max of all three now. ★THE PROPERTY GRID SCROLLS. Its last escape was not a slip and is not budgeted away: the grid is 1,160px in an 820px window, so 402px were painted where nobody can see them while `scene/pointer_reach` reported fourteen unpressable widgets. Measured after: containment 0, and `scene/scroll_reach` answers 64 marks reachable by scrolling with ZERO lost. 6/6 counterfactuals after the two findings; three were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing.

a box says where its own chrome ends, and every painter in the crate that strokes a border is asked whether it keeps its own contents inside it. Filed catalog. THE GAP WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: a scratchpad probe built against the floor at 6.11 and run offscreen reports that a titled group box there answers `3,23,3,3` for its content margins against a plain framed widget's `2,2,2,2` -- the caption band INCLUDED -- while `containment::content_rect` here subtracted only the border. So the rectangle was parity and the band was a gap, and the scene had no vocabulary in which the question could even be put. `style::Chrome` is that vocabulary: an edge, an extent, and a ROLE from a closed set whose six arms each name a strip something in this tree actually paints. The role is the half the floor cannot carry, and that is measured too rather than argued: probed there, a custom-painted widget publishes the same inset through a four-integer margin setter and reading it back gives four integers with the reason gone, so a caption band and a three pixel border are the same four numbers; and the one place the parts ARE separable is a per-class sub-control enum belonging to about twenty complex controls, which a card header or a dock tab strip is not one of. Here any painter declares a band the same way, and `scene/containment` names what a mark landed on -- `Trespass` is `outside` / `border` / `chrome:<role>`, so "this label is over the title" stops arriving as "this label is out of bounds". THE DECLARATION NEEDED A SECOND HALF AND NEITHER WORKS ALONE: `LayoutStyle::chrome_slot` says a node OCCUPIES its parent's band. Without it, declaring a caption makes every titled frame in the tree report its own title as an escape; without the declaration, whatever is drawn up there is exempt and a label that really did land on the caption goes unreported. With the pair they are two different questions -- content against the content rectangle, chrome against its own band -- and the second is not hypothetical: R1673 found a group box's legend two pixels outside its title band BY ACCIDENT, because nothing was asking. A node claiming a role its parent never reserved is judged as ordinary content rather than exempted, so a typo in a role cannot become a licence. ★★THE CRATE-LEVEL GATE IS THE ROUND'S BULK AND ITS POPULATION IS PARSED, NOT LISTED. R1673 measured fifteen painters in `pinion-widget-paint` calling `with_border` and TWO asking whether their own contents stay inside it; the other thirteen were visible only when a consumer booted, one screen at a time. `frame_gate` is the shared assertion and its census walks this crate's own syntax trees for the two calls -- a border STROKED is production code, a gate RUN is test code, and a regex over the same text cannot tell them apart (R1669's fifth census-over-text failure was exactly that). The direction is `strokes - gated`, so ADDING a bordered painter fails until it asks. There is no exception list and nowhere to put one. ★THE GATE'S FIRST RUN WAS WRONG AND THE WRONGNESS WAS THE FINDING: six painters failed, every one a label overflowing right by 8-60px, and the cause was the gate. `screen_ink`'s stand-in is deliberately wider per character than any real face, which is right for a SCREEN whose boxes are constants an author wrote down and wrong for a WIDGET that sizes its box from its content -- the box had been computed by the real shaper and the check re-measured the same string 60% wider. The ink now comes from the same `LayoutCache` the layout pass shaped with, the arrangement `scene/containment` already uses on the wire, so host font differences move the box and the ink together. What stays caught is the case where they cannot: a box pinned to a constant with a label that outgrows it. ★WHAT THE CORRECTED GATE THEN FOUND, all real, none visible to anything already running: the MENU POPUP stretched its rows across its full width over its own 1px border on both sides, in every dropdown in the tree -- and repairing it revealed a SECOND copy of the popup box in `view_context_menu` with the same defect, which is why the answer is one `popup_box` both builders call rather than two edits. Its clamp is against the OUTER size now, since clamping the content and then growing the box slides the frame back off the edge the clamp exists to keep it on. The DEVTOOLS HIGHLIGHT drew its ring UNDER the node it highlights, on three edges, while its own doc comment promised to leave that node's paint exactly as it was; the placement is `Outside` now, which is what the comment always described, and padding would have been the wrong repair because a devtools overlay that shifts what it inspects is measuring its own effect. The TOOLBAR painted its fifth control 58px past the bar, because CSS's automatic minimum size pins a content-sized flex item at its min-content width however tight the line gets; controls may shrink below their labels now and the labels elide. Six painters declared no overflow policy at all, so `TextOverflow::Visible` painted labels through their own outlines -- R1654 built those arms and no painter here had taken one. ★★THE CHECK MARK IS A PATH, which pays a debt this round's predecessor opened while fixing another: R1673 derived the tick's face from `line_box`, and `line_box` is a RESERVATION generous by ~35% because it must cover a face's ascent, descent and leading. A check mark needs none of those -- it is a shape, not a letter on a baseline -- so the M3 default tick went 18px to 12px and every checkbox in the tree shrank. A polyline has no ascent: it fits by construction, the size token means what it says again, and the commonest glyph in the catalog stops asking the host which fonts it has, which is a direct contribution to zero-flake. The stroke is inset by half its width because a round join reaches exactly that far past the polyline. ★THE ANALYZER CARD IS THE CONSUMER, and its bands are now declared rather than worked out privately: header, and footer in layout-edit mode. The first draft was ONE PIXEL OUT and the containment check found it -- the placement reserves the wider of the two border widths CONSTANTLY so rows do not shift when a card is selected, while the declaration subtracted the border actually drawn. Both sides derive from the same two constants now and a test asserts the identity in all four states, with a negative control, because the consequence is one overhang in one state and the identity holds in all of them. ★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED AND BOTH WERE THE SAME CLASS: the wire projection of both new facts had no test. Emptying `trespass` and replacing a band's role with a constant string each left the whole of `pinion-rpc` green -- and that second mutation IS the floor's behaviour, the inset surviving and the reason gone. Both are tested now with negative controls that two facts differing only in their role do not serialize alike. 18/18 counterfactuals caught after those two findings; four were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing.

SCE pin bump 60cc4fcb -> 615cb3f6 (19 commits) plus the mirror repair it forced. Declared `none`: a pin bump and its consumption check move no Phase B capability. THE CONSUMER SURFACE IS ZERO AND THAT IS MEASURED: `git diff` over `sce-rust-runtime/` is EMPTY across all nineteen commits and the new `pub` count there is 0 -- the whole delta is build-time (a W3C suite emitter, per-route backend declarations, symbol-level judgment for three runtimes, a mutation harness that can study a ctest suite). WHAT THE BUMP COST is one field, and R1657 is why it cost anything at all: upstream added `Diagnostic::expanded_from`, and `pinion-forge`'s mirror destructures that record with no `..` precisely so an upstream field addition lands as a COMPILE ERROR rather than as a claim quietly going false. It did, and this is the first bump to exercise the thing R1657 wrote down -- this tree changed nothing and its statement "I mirror the SCE v1 record shape" would have become untrue on its own. The field is classified NOT MIRRORED with its reason and the condition that would reverse it: `expanded_from` names the call site that chose the parameters when a diagnostic's `location` points at a TEMPLATE row rather than the expansion that failed, and is also upstream's signal that the value is synthetic. Pinion has no such case -- every diagnostic here names a row in a real widget chart and that row CONTAINS the `actual` it complains about, so there is no second coordinate to carry. Dual-pin discipline held: gitlink, both manifest revisions and the lock in one commit, `pin_sync.py --check-dual-pin` green, workspace 12,247 passed / 0 failed.

stop-the-line: the four CI reds are paid off, and the cause of three of them was the demo harness answering a question the framework had already answered better. Declared `none`: a repair round plus one new introspection read, with no axis re-judged against measured evidence, moves no completion number -- `scene/tag_rects` is a new capability but the api axis is judged on method STABILISATION (schemas, versioning, deprecation) and none of that moved. THE RED WAS ONE THING AND NOT WHERE THE PREVIOUS ROUND LOOKED: three data-grid demos scrubbed zero units, and driving it rather than reasoning about it showed the Count cell painted at x=-31 w=100 inside a viewport starting at x=21, so the centre a demo presses is two pixels left of anything, the press is silently dropped, and the RELEASE lands on a different cell and focuses it. ★★THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S REFUTATION WAS WRONG AND THE WAY IT WAS WRONG IS WORTH MORE THAN THE DEFECT: it removed R1673's 1px frame padding, saw the demo still FAIL, and recorded "not the cause, do not chase this again" -- re-run here, with the padding gone the demo dies in its BOOT GATE with a containment error and never reaches the scrub. Two different failures, one verdict, read as one fact. "Still failing" is not "still failing for the same reason". Also measured: even before R1673 that press point sat EXACTLY on the viewport edge, zero pixels of margin, and nothing said so. ★★THE CAUSE IS A MIRROR THAT FOLDS HALF A FACT: `abs_rects_of` re-derives where every tagged mark is painted -- deliberately, because an independent derivation is what makes a focus-ring assertion a comparison rather than a tautology -- and it folded each Scroll's OFFSET and not its CLIP, and let a LATER duplicate tag overwrite an earlier one where the framework keeps the first. `NodeVisit::absolute_rect`'s own doc argues that reported and visible have to be ONE fact because a caller that forgets the second call asserts against a rectangle nothing was drawn in; this was that caller, and nothing had ever checked that the second implementation agreed with the first. ★THE FLOOR MAKES THE SAME SPLIT, measured offscreen at 6.11 rather than argued: its item view answers x=-232 w=99 for the leading column against a 0..368 viewport, its own point-to-item lookup AGREES with that rectangle and names the cell for a point no pointer can occupy, its honest visible-region call is a widget member and an item-view cell is not a widget, and there is no enumeration in either direction. ★`scene/tag_rects` is the enumeration: every intent tag, its own rectangle and the part a pointer reaches, one round trip, `window: null` carried rather than dropped because "no such mark" and "out of sight" take different repairs. Same walk as `bbox_of_tag`, so the single lookup and the enumeration cannot disagree. ★★AND THE TWO QUESTIONS GET TWO NAMES: restoring the clip broke twenty-six demos and the sweep is what said so -- nearly all ask what the VIEW BUILT (which rows a virtualized grid windowed, which cells it asked the model for, that the newest transcript entry is painted BELOW the fold), and a node the renderer clips away is still one the view built. `unclipped_rects_of` is the second name, both readers come out of one walk, and r1445 uses BOTH, one per assertion. `_gate_tag_rects_agree` compares the whole map against the whole enumeration at every demo's boot. ★ONE ASSERTION GOT STRONGER: r1004 claimed "first match revealed at the top" while asserting source row 0 was in the band -- a claim about overdraw. Measured, rows 0-2 are painted above the viewport after that jump; it now asserts the match IS the topmost visible row. ★★THE FOURTH RED WAS A FLAKE BY CONSTRUCTION AND ITS CAUSE IS REMOVABLE: R1664 measured the software rasteriser's one-bit self-disagreement and made assertions tolerate it, with the tolerance sampled from one control pair. Measured here -- ten captures of one unchanged screen, 45 pairs: 3 byte-identical by default, 45 of 45 with the tile count pinned to one. So it is thread interleaving. A control pair agreeing by luck reports a floor of 0 and then fails a tested pair that noised by 1, which is exactly the green-local/red-CI shape; and a tolerance of 1 hides a stale fragment differing by one bit, so removing the noise gives the assertion its strength back. Pinned where the binary is LAUNCHED rather than in the CI job, because a repro on a developer machine has to have the property CI has. ★TWO MORE REDS WERE R1674's: it added `chrome` to the facet census and to the wire and did not move the two demos that restate the key set independently -- which is what those restatements are for, and they fired. The sharper demand was the second: a facet no binding can be seen DECLARING is a key whose presence is untested, and neither binding declared a chrome band, so a third one that does was added. 4/4 counterfactuals caught.

the analyzer's node-graph screen says what it can be asked to DO, and a gate drives every declared way of asking. Filed dcc; no completion re-judged, because the round adds verifiability and two reads rather than a widget. ★★WHY A CENSUS OF THE PAINT COULD NOT FIND THIS: the specification describes panes, roles, cards, fields and a hint strip, and the forward/backward sweep compares the painted scene against all of it -- but an operation the screen does not answer PAINTS NOTHING, so there is no tag to look for and no run to measure. The blind spot is measured rather than estimated: the reference prototype publishes its own operation list and measures its own coverage against it, so the population is ITS declaration, and against those thirty this screen answered seven outright and sixteen not at all while every check here was green. ★★TWO COLUMNS OF CAUSE, BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE THE DEFECTS LIVE: every failure a person reported on this screen had one shape -- the screen advertises an operation, an agent driving the wire gets it, and the pointer does not (a wheel that zooms through an action and not through the wheel hook, a form row whose press resolves to a named target and falls through an unhandled arm, a frame that drags without selecting). One column hides all of them because the column that works is the one a test naturally drives. So an operation declares the ACTION an agent invokes and whether a PERSON has a way in, and the gate drives both -- the second through the screen's own pointer handlers, aimed at rectangles read out of the painted scene, never by writing the state, because a state a test invents can be one no mouse can reach. ★ABSENT IS A ROW, NOT A GAP: an operation with no verb and no gesture is written down, which is what lets it be counted, ratcheted and FALSIFIED -- a row claimed absent that turns out to work fails as loudly as one claimed present that does not. ★★★WHAT THE FIRST RUN FOUND, six of eighteen declared ways causing nothing, split three ways. THREE WERE A SILENCE ON THE WIRE: moving a node, moving a frame and re-parenting between frames each had a gesture and NO OBSERVABLE RESULT -- canvas positions lived only inside the document and frame membership was witnessed by a toast sentence, so an agent driving any of the three could not observe its own drag, and a gesture whose effect cannot be read is indistinguishable from one that did nothing. That is precisely how "the frame drags but does not select" survived. `layout` and `frames` are published reads now, in CANVAS coordinates because that is the question a caller placing or comparing nodes asks, with `scene/tag_rects` answering the window question for the same cards. ONE WAS THE DECLARATION GATE DOING ITS JOB: both new reads answered `UnknownIntrospectPath` first, because since R1637 the schema declaration is a PRECONDITION of dispatch and not a description of it. TWO WERE THE TABLE BEING OPTIMISTIC AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE MEASUREMENTS: the integer stepper cannot cause an edit on the opening screen because its field is already at its ceiling, so a driver aimed there clamps; and `validate` has NO pointer path at all -- the verdict is derived, causing it means crossing a bound, the stepper correctly refuses and the text rows have no pointer path, so an agent can close the launch gate and a person cannot. Written down rather than assumed away. ★THE COUNT IS EIGHTEEN AND THE READING THAT MOTIVATED THIS SAID SIXTEEN, kept visible rather than reconciled: that reading was three-way and "partly" is a judgement, this is binary and mechanical, and two rows it called partly answered have neither way in (the configuration export says how many keys there are without exporting them; the launch script does not exist). 4/4 counterfactuals caught -- a declared gesture with no driver, a press that never presses, a witness pointed at a slot its verb cannot move, and a ratchet number drifted from the table.

the settings form gains the mirror `settle` never had, and the analyzer's node-graph screen gains the reset family its reference has and it had none of. Filed catalog: `ConfigForm` is a crate widget, so `revert` / `edited` reach every consumer. ★★THE SHAPE IS MEASURED, NOT REMEMBERED: extracting the reference's markup rather than recalling it settles two things a guess gets wrong -- four of its five reset affordances are wrapped in a CONDITIONAL on a per-scope "has this changed" predicate, so a reset with nothing to put back is not disabled but ABSENT, and the fifth (the view) sits unconditionally beside the zoom controls. That asymmetry is a judgement worth keeping: pan and zoom always have a home, while a graph reset appearing out of nowhere over an untouched screen is an invitation to destroy work. ★★★THE REFERENCE DOES EACH RESET IN ONE LINE BECAUSE OF A STRUCTURAL CHOICE, and seeing it is the round's content: it keeps every edit as an OVERLAY on the opening state, so a reset is one clear and "is there anything to put back" is one is_empty. This tree mutates in place, so both facts are derived by comparing against the SPECIFICATION -- which is where the opening state comes from, so there is no snapshot to fall out of step. The two halves are ONE TYPE (`changed` / `apply`) because a screen deciding for itself when to show a "put it back" affordance is a second author of the rule, and that failure is silent in both directions: a button over an unchanged screen does nothing when pressed, a missing one strands the change. ★★THE SUBSTRATE HAD THE ASYMMETRY WRITTEN INTO IT AND NOBODY HAD NAMED IT: `ConfigField::settle` has existed since R1651 -- accept the current value as the one this form opened with -- and there was no way back. `revert` is its mirror and `edited` is the question it answers. The MEMBERSHIP half is not decoration and a value-only baseline is exactly what this type had: a row ADDED after the form opened is NOT edited (its value is its original) and a row REMOVED is not there to be asked, and both are changes. `opened_with` carries KEYS rather than a copy of the rows, because add and remove only MOVE a field between the held and offered sets so the union is invariant; the opening ORDER is restored too, which a set-based repair loses and which is what a reader navigates a form by. `settle` now accepts the shape as well as the values, because a launch means "what is running now IS what the screen shows". ★★THE GATE LEARNED A REAL PROPERTY OF THE TOOL: R1677's operation gate drives every declared way from a FRESH screen, and a reset cannot be caused from a fresh screen at all -- there is nothing to put back and its affordance is not painted. That is not an awkwardness to route around, it is WHY the reference gates those four buttons. `OperationSpec::needs` names the operation that has to have run first and the gate reaches it the way a person would, by doing the earlier thing and preferring its GESTURE where it has one; a setup that wrote the state directly would let a reset be proven against a state no session can produce. A `needs` naming an operation the table does not hold fails, and one whose target has no way in at all fails too -- an unreachable precondition would silently stop exercising the operation that declared it. ★THE BACKWARD CHECK GREW ONE NEW IDEA: the four conditional affordances are tags that are legitimately absent, so the specification names precisely the buttons that must exist at any given moment rather than declaring a family that may or may not be there. That makes the in-process check unable to see a `changed_scopes` that always answered yes -- the paint and the specification both read it -- and the DEMO is what catches it, asserting from outside that a gated affordance is absent on the opening screen. Measured: the counterfactual that makes every affordance unconditional is caught there and NOWHERE ELSE. ★WHAT DID NOT COME ACROSS, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO A DIFF: the reference counts an edit made and then undone as a change because its overlay still holds the key, while a comparison says the screen is back where it started and hides the button -- the button's job is to put something back, so the derived answer is the one kept. And its view reset goes to 100% while this one goes to the zoom the SCREEN specification opens at; "reset" means "back to how it opened" in both and the two files disagree about what that is. `seed_links` lifted out of `opening` because a reset re-authors those links and the accept-pin run arithmetic must not exist twice. `ABSENT_OPERATIONS` 18 -> 13. 4/4 counterfactuals caught.

every debt this session opened is paid, and paying two of them found defects neither debt note knew about. Filed catalog: the repairs land in the settings-form crate and in the analyzer screen's own gates. ★★★THE AFFORDANCE GATE FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, WHICH IS WHY IT HAD TO STOP ASKING THE PREDICATE: R1678's counterfactual showed that making `changed_scopes` always answer yes left all thirty-six in-process checks GREEN, because the paint and the specification both derive from that one function and therefore move together. The repair is not a second copy of the predicate -- it is to judge by RESULT: in every swept state, for every gated scope, take the witness, apply the reset, take it again, assert the button was painted IFF the value moved. Nothing in that test knows what the predicate answers. Its first run reported the LINK reset as changing the screen in all eight states including the opening one, where the affordance was correctly absent: the reset cleared every link and re-authored the set, and the model assigns a fresh identifier to each new link, so putting an UNTOUCHED graph back renumbered all seven. The reference's reset is idempotent because it drops an overlay that is already empty; this one now earns it by DIFFING -- removing only what the specification lacks, adding only what is missing, so a link nobody touched keeps its identity. It deliberately does NOT consult `changed`, because an apply that early-returned on "nothing differs" would make the new gate compare the predicate with itself. ★★THE LAYOUT REPAIR WAS UNPROVABLE UNTIL A COUNTERFACTUAL SAID SO, AND THE REASON WAS A SILENT NO-OP: the predicate's population was the specification's node list, so a card the palette added could be dragged anywhere and the screen reported its layout unchanged; it now compares every card against where it CAME INTO BEING, recorded at creation (from the specification for the opening cards, from the placement arithmetic for an added one) because a card the specification does not describe has no other source. The swept states had no state where an added card is dragged -- which the debt note itself had said -- and adding one was not enough: the first draft aimed the drag with `card_rect`, which answers in the WORLD SURFACE's coordinates while `move_cursor` takes the WINDOW's, so the press went nowhere, the state was a no-op, and the counterfactual for the very defect it was written for PASSED. ★AND THAT STATE EXPOSED A STRUCTURAL FACT: the swept states have two consumers with opposite assumptions -- the painted sweeps apply them cumulatively (state n is state n-1 plus one edit) while the operation and affordance gates reset before each, because their rows must be independent. A state leaning on an earlier one for the card it drags passed three tests and panicked in the fourth; it is self-contained now and the reason is written where the next author will be standing. ★THE OTHER TWO ARE TRIPWIRES PUT WHERE THE COST BELONGS: the facet census gains a test beside itself that reads both demos' hand-written restatements and fails when they drift -- those restatements stay hand-written ON PURPOSE, since their job is to fail when the projection and the type drift TOGETHER and a list derived from the wire would agree with the wire by construction, so only the moment of discovery moves, from a CI run to the commit that caused it. And the two rect readers: MEASURED first (25 demos read the placement reader, NONE aims a press with it) then held there by an AST taint check in the harness suite pre-push already runs, because aiming a press with the placement reader re-creates exactly what R1676 paid off. What that check cannot see -- a rect through a parameter or a container -- is stated in it rather than left to be discovered by getting away with it. 5/5 counterfactuals caught, two of them after a first attempt that PASSED or did not compile and taught something either way.

the push was refused, and the red it refused over was NOT the one this session had paid off. Filed catalog: the repair is in a catalogue widget. ★★★STOP-THE-LINE DID ITS JOB AND SO DID THIS SESSION'S OWN LESSON: R1676 paid off five CI reds, all in the demo sweep, and the gate still refused because the last completed run failed. The tempting read is "that is the red I fixed, override and go"; the entry two rounds earlier says why not -- "still failing" is not "still failing for the same reason". Reading the run took ONE call: the failing job is `workspace tests`, not the sweep, and the failing test is one R1674 ADDED. ★★THE DEBT THAT PREDICTED IT WAS REGISTERED ONE ROUND EARLIER: R1674.1's close audit found the zero-flake claim in `frame_gate`'s doc only half true -- the font moves a box and its ink TOGETHER for a content-sized box and not for a fixed one -- and measured ten of fifteen painters pinning a fixed box with no overflow policy. The next CI run turned that exposure into a red. Reproduced rather than reasoned about: with this host's fonts the gate is green, and with FONTCONFIG_FILE at the runner's DejaVu-only set "Undo" overhangs by 2 left and 1 right and "Redo" by 1 each side -- the same instrument R1660 built for the ink ratchet, one layer down. ★★★THE CAUSE IS A POLICY APPLIED TO THE WRONG BOX, AND THAT IS THE GENERAL FORM: `TextOverflow::Ellipsis` shortens a run to fit ITS OWN rect, taffy gives a flex child its content width and `JustifyContent::Center` centres it, so a child WIDER than its parent still has a rect it fits exactly -- the policy never fires and the ink spills out both sides. R1674 released the CONTROL's automatic minimum size so a crowded bar could shrink it and left the LABEL at its own, so the control got narrower and the text box did not. The repair is the same release one level down: the label may shrink below its content, taffy clamps the text box to the control, and the elide policy finally has the right rectangle to shorten against. ★THE CLASS IS NOT CLOSED AND IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN CLAIMED -- nobody has counted how many painters centre a text child without releasing its minimum size; the toolbar is the one CI found. The entry plan starts with a PARSER census rather than a grep and names the deeper repair: letting `TextOverflow` see the parent's content box, so "which box is this policy about" becomes the framework's answer instead of each painter's. ★AND THE GATE THAT FOUND IT CANNOT FIND THE REST HERE: `frame_gate` measures with the HOST's fonts, so this whole class stays green locally and turns red elsewhere. The reproduction path exists and is written down; wiring it into a run somebody actually performs is that debt's work, not a claim made here. Verified under BOTH font sets and with `--no-fail-fast`, because cargo's default stops at the first failing test binary and a second font-dependent failure would have been invisible behind this one. ★★AND THE PUSH DEMANDED A RE-JUDGMENT OF THIS AXIS, WHICH HOLDS AT 98 — folded into this round's row rather than declared as its own, because a re-judgment advances no axis (R1604) and this round's row already names the axis it repaired; the number did not move, so nothing credits itself for being looked at. DEMANDED by the tool at the push (round-axis 16 -> 22, +38%). ★HOLDING STILL IS THE HONEST OUTCOME AND THE TOOL ASKS FOR A LOOK, NOT A MOVE: six rounds declared this axis since R1672 and every one added CORRECTNESS to widgets the catalogue already has, not surface it lacks -- a box says where its own chrome ends and all fifteen bordered painters are asked whether they keep their contents inside it (R1674), the check mark became a path so the commonest glyph in the catalogue stopped asking the host which fonts it has, the settings form gained `revert` and `edited` (the mirror `settle` never had, covering values AND rows added or taken away, R1678), and a toolbar label may finally shrink below its own text so the elide policy fires against the box that actually constrains it (R1680). ★★THE NAMED GAPS ARE RE-MEASURED AND UNMOVED, WHICH IS WHAT DECIDES IT: `External::wheel` still has exactly TWO implementors in the widget catalogue -- `slider` and `spin_button`, the same two since R1554 -- so the largest cross-cutting item is where it was, and the analyzer's node canvas hitting it from a consumer screen this session (its hint strip advertises a wheel zoom no wheel answers) is evidence the gap is REAL rather than evidence it shrank. The four absent widget kinds are still four. A round that improves a widget the tree already has creates no artifact, which is why this ledger exists; what it cannot do is turn depth into breadth.

a link's life after it is drawn: the node-graph crate gains an identity-preserving `relink`, and the analyzer's node-graph screen gains delete, re-aim, choose-an-endpoint and adopt. Filed dcc: `Document::relink` is crate surface every node system reaches, and the highest-leverage axis is the one it sits on. ★★★THE VERB IS NOT DISCONNECT-THEN-CONNECT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED: `connect` mints an identifier, so a link taken out and put back is a NEW link and everything holding the old name -- a selection, a breakpoint, an undo entry, a renderer's cache -- is holding a dangling one. This session watched that from the other side one round earlier, when a reset rebuilt its links and silently changed a screen that should not have moved. So the link comes out, the graph is vetted WITHOUT it, and it goes back under its own id, its own mute and its own place in the order; a refusal puts it back exactly as it was and returns the reason intact. The counterfactual that mints a new id is caught by six tests, and the demo catches it end to end. ★★THE FLOOR WAS PROBED RATHER THAN RECALLED, offscreen against the reference toolkit's own relocation verb: a persistent handle SURVIVES an in-place relocation and is INVALIDATED by remove-plus-insert -- which is why that verb exists at all -- but it is offered only over a FLAT sequence, the structural model inherits the base class's `false`, and a refusal carries one bit. A graph is neither a list nor a tree, and "no" is not a reason. ★★AN ENDPOINT BELONGS TO THE LINK, NOT THE NODE, which is the reference's own first sentence about it: a target listening in two places can be dialled two ways, and which one a wire took is a property of the wire. Here that is the accept run's ITEM -- one slot per arriving link, labelled with the address it dials and TYPED by that address's transport -- so choosing an endpoint is the same `relink` over a different socket, and dialling an address this link cannot speak is refused by the model with both transports named. The reference sets an index and checks nothing. ★A COUNTERFACTUAL PASSED AND THE HEADER WAS CORRECTED RATHER THAN THE CODE: lifting the link before the VET rather than merely before the placement is not observable today -- the four vetting rules are provably blind to the link being moved in an acyclic graph, since a cycle through it would have to reach its producing node before arriving at its consuming one. Structural rather than a bad constant -- a card shrinks with the zoom while a column derived from a type size with a legibility floor under it does not -- so the column is placed where it fits, and is kept inside what the canvas is showing, because the first draft nudged both endpoint seats out of the visible world entirely. ★THE FOUR DRIVERS PRESS WHAT A PERSON PRESSES: a wire is a PATH and a path's painted rectangle is its bounding box, whose centre is nowhere near the stroke, so the aim comes from the two things that do have rectangles -- the pins the wire runs between. And a link is named on the wire by its ENDS rather than by an id, because an id is minted in seeding order and a table asserting `3` asserts something about the order the screen happened to author its opening graph in. `ABSENT_OPERATIONS` 13 -> 9. 8/8 counterfactuals caught.

a node's life after it is placed: the node-graph crate gains an identity-preserving rename and a switch that is not a bypass, and the analyzer's node-graph screen gains delete, rename, collapse and switch-off. Filed dcc: `Document::relabel` and `Document::set_disabled` are crate surface every node system reaches, and this is the highest-leverage axis. ★★★A RENAME IS NOT A RE-CREATION, AND THE COST OF PRETENDING OTHERWISE IS MEASURED: the behaviour reference has no rename, so it copies the node under the new name and covers the old one with a deletion -- and then hand-moves TEN side tables to compensate (placement, containment, edits, extra fields, hidden fields, collapse, mute, wire list, selection, draft). Here the node keeps its identifier and the edit moves one string, so the list of things a rename must carry is EMPTY, and that emptiness is the assertion rather than the claim: the form, the placement, the frame, the degree and every link id are compared across the rename. ★★THE FLOOR WAS PROBED OFFSCREEN RATHER THAN RECALLED: against the reference toolkit's own naming surface, an object's identity DOES survive a rename -- but naming a second sibling what the first is called is ACCEPTED, both then hold it, its singular by-name lookup answers an arbitrary one of the two and says nothing, its item model accepts a duplicate display string the same way, and the rename notification carries exactly ONE argument which is the NEW name. So a listener holding a table keyed by the old one is told that something changed and not what to un-key. Two things follow and both are strictly better: a name another node answers to is REFUSED with the holder named, so authored names are unique within a tree and the by-name lookup is a FUNCTION; and the edit ANSWERS the old name, which costs nothing because it was already in hand. Where the invariant is broken from outside the verb -- the field is public -- the singular lookup declines to guess and a plural one says which of the two failures it was, since "nothing answers to this" and "several do" are different problems with different fixes. ★★SWITCHING A NODE OFF IS NOT BYPASSING IT, and the difference is what reaches the nodes downstream: a bypassed node stops computing and its inputs travel straight through, so the graph below carries on; a disabled one produces nothing, so everything that depended on it reads nothing. An editor needs both -- "route around this" and "switch this off" are different intentions -- and a model with only the first makes the second unsayable, which is how it ends up in application state where no derivation can see it. Driven through the evaluator rather than read off the flags, including the one path it could still have leaked through: a disabled source does not hand out its own AUTHORED value either. It deliberately does NOT cascade through containment the way the reference toolkit's enabled-ness cascades through its widget tree, because the relation along which "this is not running" travels in a graph is the FLOW, and the flow cascade is derived rather than authored. ★★THE SCREEN'S SECOND NAME FOR A CARD WAS LIFTED AWAY, AND RENAMING IS WHAT MADE IT LOAD-BEARING: it kept a name-to-node map beside the document's own label, two records of one fact, and a rename updating either alone leaves the canvas and the wire calling one card two things. The document owns names now -- it is the thing that can refuse one -- so there is one record and no way to update half of it. ★★★AND THE RENAME FORCED A DEFECT OUT OF THE RESET IT HAD NOTHING TO DO WITH: the node reset told an opening card from a palette-added one by asking whether its NAME is in the specification, which is exactly the thing a rename changes -- so a renamed opening card read as a stray and the reset that exists to PUT ITS NAME BACK would have deleted the node instead. A card is a stray when nothing recorded it opening; the record already existed (R1679 added it for the layout predicate) and gains the name the card came into being as. Nothing was aimed at that row; giving the form somewhere to type answered it. ★★★THE INSPECTOR HAD TWO COORDINATE TRANSFORMS AND THE FORM WAS ONE PIXEL OUT, up and left, to the hit test and to assistive technology both: every other rectangle in that pane goes through `in_body`, which includes the panel frame the scrolling body is drawn inside, and the form geometry wrote `pane.origin - offset` on its own. R791.1 audited that exact duplication and deferred it because the scene walk lives in `pinion_runtime::rect_for_tag` and the paint crate deliberately does not depend on pinion-runtime; that premise is FALSE -- `rect_for_tag` is a one-line wrapper over `Scene::rect_for_tag_absolute`, a method on the scene type the paint crate already has, so the dependency the defer protected against was never needed. `ime_caret_rect_in_scene` and `byte_for_scene_point` now own the walk and eleven call sites lost four lines each; what stays binding-side is the FOCUS GUARD, which is policy rather than composition (the analyzer screen answers "was this press mine" by geometry where every sibling answers it by tag, because all its presses reach one root external). a box can say that what does not fit in it is cut there: `LayoutStyle::overflow` lands as one declaration carrying both halves, and the clip stops being a property of a node KIND. Filed catalog because there is no layout axis and what this closes is catalog-class — a control whose label must stop at the control, and a screen whose chrome holds while its body yields. ★★★THE CONSUMER REPORT WAS RIGHT AND THE HALVES WERE SPLIT: `overflow: hidden` is one CSS word and this tree could express only its layout half (`min_size: Px(0)`, which relaxes the same automatic minimum size and is documented as doing so), while the paint half existed ONLY on `Scene::Scroll`. A region that had to cut its overflow therefore had to become scrollable, or have its pixel budget balanced by hand — and a consumer read the min_size documentation, concluded the port had happened, and hit the wall at the far end of the work. taffy has carried `Style.overflow` all along; not lowering it is what made the two halves two things. ★★★THE CLIP IS NOW A FACT ABOUT A NODE, NOT ABOUT A VARIANT: `Scene::clip_window` is the single reading, `SceneNodeKind::clips_subtree` becomes `can_clip_subtree` (the kind half — it holds children at all, asserted against `child_nodes` rather than restated), and every consumer that had spelled `matches!(node, Scene::Scroll(_))` asks the node instead: the walk's clip fold, both vello walkers, the cell walker, the PDF projector, `containment`'s fate and `reach`'s viewport chain. CSS's own rule is what makes that fall out of one arithmetic instead of a special case: content overflowing a hidden box does not contribute to a scroll region, so the box's own extent is its scroll region. ★★★THE ADOPTION FOUND A FRAME BUG THE UNIT TESTS COULD NOT: the toolbar's controls declare the cut (R1674 and R1680 had each spelled its layout half by hand, and R1680's CI red was INK past the box, which no minimum and no elide can reach because `TextOverflow` shortens a run to fit the rect it was measured into). R1676 built that cross-check for exactly this, and it worked. ★A NEW BINDING IS THE REPORT'S OWN SHAPE — header, yielding body, action bar, tab bar, with the entries taller than the body at the size it opens in — and the demo drives all four claims over the wire: the declaration on `scene/snapshot`, the chrome heights at three window sizes, `scene/containment` calling the cut `clipped` and never `smeared`, `scene/scroll_reach` calling it `lost` with the body named and its range zero, and `scene/locate` landing on the band that IS painted there. ★AND LOOKING AT THE WINDOW CHANGED IT: every gate was green while the entries and the body shared a fill, so the half-cut card — the whole picture — was invisible. 11/11 counterfactuals caught, two only after the edit was made compilable and one only after the instrument was repaired.

what leaves the screen: the graph says how it is brought up, and the settings form says what it could not express. The analyser table had carried `export the configuration` and `produce the launch script` as absent on BOTH channels since R1677, the last two of the behaviour reference's own "what leaves the screen" group. Filed dcc because the config form IS the property-grid family and the order is node-graph substrate. ★★★THE REFERENCE WRITES THEM AS ONE GROUP AND IT IS RIGHT TO: they are one derivation rendered twice -- the launch order, each node's configuration document, and the rows the document could not carry -- so building either alone means building the derivation and using half of it, and the unused half is the one that then drifts. A test holds that: the script writes its files in the order the document publishes, and a counterfactual that sorted one of them by name fails in both layers. ★★★★★THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE ORDER WAS WRONG AND THE MODEL SAID SO. It bucketed nodes by "is dialled / dials out" and justified skipping a topological walk with "two peers that dial each other are a legal mesh, so no such order exists". BOTH HALVES WERE FALSE: `connect` refuses a cycle outright, so an authored tree is acyclic by construction and mutual reachability lives in the OBSERVED layer, which is not authored and not deployed. With the excuse gone the bucketing was simply incorrect -- in a chain of four the middle two share a bucket and a NAME decides their order while the links demand the reverse -- and the first fixture was three deep, where the buckets are right by luck. Kahn's walk over the reversed link direction, with the four words kept as the reported REASON a node sits where it does, which is what a reader wants and what the order alone cannot say. ★★A NODE SWITCHED OFF IS NOT STARTED, AND ITS LINKS GO WITH IT -- two claims, and the second is the one a fixture misses: with the middle of a chain off, the two ends never dialled each other, so they are ordered by name and not by a constraint neither of them has. ★★★★★THE SUBSTRATE FINDING IS AN ASYMMETRY THAT HAD BEEN THERE SINCE R1651: the settings form's READ half is total and says so in its own documentation -- `adopt` places every leaf or NAMES it in `Adopted::unplaceable`, "nothing is dropped quietly", because a configuration written by a newer target is the normal case -- and the WRITE half was all-or-nothing. One unparseable row and `document()` hands back an error instead of the other forty rows, which are fine and are what somebody asked for. Invisible while the only caller was a launch gate, because a gate only ever wants the yes-or-no. `ConfigForm::compose` is the total form and `document` is now its NARROWING rather than a second walk, so the pair a caller most needs to trust -- "is this shippable" and "what did not fit" -- cannot disagree. ★★★★★AND A COUNTERFACTUAL PROVED MY OWN SYMMETRY TEST PARTLY VACUOUS: because `document` is DERIVED from `compose`, a `compose` that silently swallowed a defective row moved both sides together -- the row vanishes, `unexpressed` is empty, `complete()` is true, `document` answers Ok, and the two agree on the wrong thing. What caught it was R1651's pre-existing test with a hard-coded expectation. The check now compares the unexpressed rows against `defects()`, which reaches the fields by its own path, and re-running the same counterfactual turns 2 failures into 3. That is the assertion-compared-with-itself class R1681.1, R1682 and R1684.1 each met somewhere else. ★★★THE `unexpressed` POPULATION IS SMALLER THAN THE REFERENCE'S AND THAT IS THE MODEL, NOT A GAP: the reference has two sources -- a value that cannot be encoded, and a row that is not a configuration path at all -- and `ConfigField` is declared with the key BEING the path, verbatim, so there is no second kind of row to fall out. Inventing a table of run-only keys would be inventing the distinction the form was designed without. ★★★★LOOKING AT THE RUNNING SCREEN FOUND A DEFECT NO GATE WAS ASKING ABOUT: the view-reset seat painted `ho…` for `home`. Measured rather than eyeballed -- `scene/text_painted` reports seven shortened runs and six are long sentences elided into bounded strips, which is what that behaviour is for; a control's own NAME is the case where it is a defect. ★★★★★AND THE COUNTERFACTUAL FOR THE GATE THAT REPAIR EARNED WALKED STRAIGHT THROUGH IT: narrowing the seat to prove the check fired did NOT fire it, because the captions were authored as their own constants -- `home` in a 40-wide box on a 34-wide seat, `config` in a 60-wide box on a 66-wide seat inset 12 -- so two of three were painted PAST the button they name, and a caption outside its seat neither elides nor sits inside the rectangle the check asks about. The check went quiet on the worse of the two defects. Captions are derived from the seat now (`seat_caption`), the gate asks BOTH questions -- inside, and not cut -- and generalising it from "is it cut" to "is it inside the control it names" immediately found a third: the zoom readout was painted two pixels inside the `+` button. ★★★THE TOOLBAR'S DECLARED WIDTH WAS A SENTENCE NOBODY READ AND HAD BEEN WRONG SINCE R1678: `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER` said 300 while the view-reset seat R1678 added sits 340 in. That is [[debt-a-stated-limit-is-not-checked-by-anything]] exactly -- a limit in prose is re-derived by whoever is next and the original is never re-read. It is measured now, from the rectangles themselves, on BOTH halves rather than only the one this round's defect was in, and the window's floor is asserted to be their sum. THE COST IS REAL AND IS STATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED: one button took the minimum window from 1316 to 1442, so a 1366-wide laptop no longer shows this screen unclipped, and the gate is what makes that somebody's decision instead of arithmetic nobody sees. ★★TWO DEMOS WERE CARRYING THEIR OWN COPY OF THAT FLOOR and failed on a fact about the screen rather than on a defect; the specification publishes it now, for the same reason it publishes the operations table. ★★★★THE WHOLE TOOLBAR WAS SILENT TO ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY: asking whether the two new seats were named found that NONE of them were -- a screen reader could be told the launch gate's verdict, which rides in the group's value, and not that there was a button for it. The roster is the whole cluster and not the two this round added, because a gate placed where the last defect was finds only the last defect. ★THE READ SLOT IS `produced` AND NOT `export`, which the wire settled before a reader would have: `export` is an ACTION, one address on two channels is refused as `PathIsAReadSlot`, and the slot holds BOTH artifacts -- so pressing `script` would have changed a slot called `export`. ★DCC RE-JUDGED AND IT HOLDS AT 88, demanded by `round-axis` +28%: the census was re-run rather than carried (the DCC 58/76, the engine 132/211, identical to R1663), and this round's own node-graph work is deliberately uncounted because neither reference DEPLOYS a graph -- the capability is real and the meter is blind to it, which is the disagreement [[debt-the-dcc-axis-measures-three-of-its-four-families]] already registers, seen from a new side. 8/8 counterfactuals caught, two of them only after the test or the paint they demanded was repaired.
