where the canvas is pointed: framing the whole graph, and going to the first thing wrong with it. The analyser table's LAST two absences, so the count reaches zero for the first time -- and neither was difficult, which is the argument for the column existing: a census of what is ON a screen is blind by construction to what the screen cannot DO, so eleven rounds of green sweeps sat over these two. Filed dcc because what actually landed is node-graph substrate. ★★★★★TWO NODE CANVASES IN THIS TREE HAD WRITTEN THE SAME AFFINE BY HAND: `hello-node-editor` frames its graph by folding a union box, dividing the window by it, clamping into a zoom range and pinning the centre, and `hello-node-lab` was about to write a fourth coordinate conversion of its own to do the same. So `pinion_node_graph::view` is `Camera` (one projection with its own inverse, plus `pinned` -- "put this graph point under this pixel" -- which `zoomed_at` and every viewport write are call shapes of), `ZoomRange` (validated where it is built, so no clamp is ever asked to order two numbers that are not ordered), `Margin` and `Fit`. Both canvases call it; the editor's `frame_all`, its cursor-anchored zoom and both of its projections are now that module, and its own viewport demos are part of this round's gate. ★★★★THE MARGIN DECLARES ITS FRAME OF REFERENCE, WHICH A SINGLE NUMBER CANNOT: `Margin::Canvas` pads the graph's box in graph units so the clearance scales with the diagram, `Margin::Screen` keeps a gutter in pixels so it is the same at every zoom. They produce different scales for one graph, the behaviour canon this tree reproduces uses the first and the DCC "frame selection" idiom uses the second, and both consumers here want the one they want. ★★★A FIT SAYS WHETHER IT FITTED. `Fitted::complete` is false when the zoom floor cannot shrink the graph into the pane -- the one case where the button did not do what it says, and the case the reference toolkit's own fit returns `void` for. ★★★★★AND `card_shape_at` IS WHY THE FIT IS A FUNCTION OF THE GRAPH RATHER THAN OF THE VIEW: a card's box is DERIVED from the zoom it is drawn at (the faces have a legibility floor and the rows collapse below it, both deliberate), so measuring what is on screen and dividing the zoom back out makes "frame the graph" depend on where you were already looking -- press it from two zooms, get two cameras. The scale is a parameter now, the extent is asked at 100%, and the counterfactual that reads the live zoom fails two tests. THE FIRST DRAFT DID EXACTLY THAT FOR THE HOST FRAMES and the idempotence test caught it a pixel at a time. ★★★THE JUMP'S AFFORDANCE IS THE LAUNCH CHIP, which had been on screen saying the verdict and answering no press at all -- the reference's own design, and it cost the toolbar no width, which mattered because the toolbar is what sets this screen's minimum window. `LabState::problems` is the one walk: the panel had been formatting a card's name INTO a sentence and returning the sentence, so "take me to the first one" was unanswerable without parsing the name back out. ★★THE ZOOM PILL IS THE REFERENCE'S NOW -- minus, the read-out, plus, fit -- and the READ-OUT IS THE VIEW RESET, which is what the reference makes it: this screen had a number that could not be pressed beside a seat captioned `home` that the reference does not have. Merging them is one control for one subject and it costs less width than the two did, which is the difference between adding the fit seat and not being able to. ★★★★THE ROSTER: `toolbar_seats` is the ONE list the hit test finds a press in, the accessibility tree names, and the width gate measures. R1687 derived that gate's requirement from rectangles -- a real improvement over the prose it replaced -- but from a list of seven written inside the test, and this round added an eighth seat that list did not have: green, and blind to the very change it was written for. A seat that is not in the roster now fails to COMPILE, because the roster is the only constructor of the toolbar's hits. ★★★★★LOOKING AT THE SCREEN FOUND A CAPABILITY STATED AND UNBUILT FOR THIRTY-SEVEN ROUNDS: four comments in this file say a refusal "has already reached the toast, which is where a person reads it", and there was no toast. `say` wrote a signal, the signal was published on the wire, and nothing painted it -- so every gate was green because every gate reads the wire, while the last card refusing to be deleted and a name already taken were controls that appeared to do nothing. It is painted now, above the hint strip and left of the launch panel, and it does NOT time out: a message that vanishes on a wall clock makes every check that reads it a race, and it is also the complaint people have about toasts. ★★★R1687 LEFT `WIN_W` BELOW `MIN_W` and nothing said so -- the shell was asked to open a window narrower than the minimum handed over in the same call, and every headless probe laid the screen out at a width the screen says it does not support, surviving on two pixels of slack. The design size follows the floor by construction now, asserted at COMPILE time (a runtime check for it is `assert!(true)`, which clippy says and which is the lesson R1644.1 wrote down), and what the tests assert is the pair the shell is actually handed. ★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED AND BOTH BECAME TESTS: taking the host frames out of the fit changed nothing observable, because a frame reaches 32 units past its members and the fit pads by 60 -- a silent dependency on one constant exceeding two others -- so the choice is now stated where it can fail, as the fitted box being strictly larger than the cards' own on every side. And swapping the editor's screen margin for a canvas one left every test AND the R877 demo green, because that fit only asserted a zoom BAND; the margin is pinned as what it means now, EXACTLY rather than within a pixel, because the two kinds differ by one pixel here and the first draft's tolerance let the wrong arm through. ★★THAT TEST ALSO SURFACED A PRE-EXISTING LIMIT: `frame_all` cannot centre vertically when the fit wants a negative pan, because a scroll offset floors at zero -- measured at 26 px high, and now an assertion rather than a sentence nobody would read again. ★A SYSTEM-DEPENDENCY DECLARATION WAS MISSING, reported by a consumer building on a clean machine: `sce-build` build-depends on the `libxml` crate, which probes `pkg-config libxml-2.0` and then runs bindgen, so `libxml2-dev` and `libclang-dev` are on the path of every workspace build and were declared nowhere. Invisible because every machine this tree had been built on already had both for other reasons -- a declaration only ever read on machines that satisfy it is a coincidence, not a declaration. 17 counterfactuals, 15 caught outright, 2 passed and turned into the tests above. Local gates: 3 crates green, 10 node-lab demos + 4 node-editor viewport demos green, and the screen was looked at in a window three times. ★★★★★R1688.1 PAID OFF R1687's CI RED, WHICH WAS NOT A FLAKY DEMO: `r1182_node_edge_autopan` read a 1:1 ride by subtracting two separate RPC queries of a thing that is moving, and reading them in the other order changes the answer by 27 px. Measured while repairing it: `scene/set_fps 0` does NOT stop the pan -- with pacing confirming `fps: 0`, one read plus one second of WALL CLOCK plus one read moves the viewport 796 px, which contradicts what that call documents and is registered as its own debt. Reading the ride from the PAINT instead, in one call, then showed excursions of 4-11 px about one run in six, and those were a real tearing defect: `AutoPan::tick` wrote the scroll offset and the dragged nodes as two separate signal writes, so a frame landing between them painted a world that had scrolled and a node that had not followed -- in an editor whose `apply_viewport` already batches for exactly that reason and cites the rule. One batch, plus a tolerance DERIVED from the pan rate and the rounding chain rather than fitted, and the demo is 15/15 then 10/10. The teeth are proven, not assumed: a follow at half rate slides the node off the canvas entirely.

the analyzer node screen's graph survives being closed, and an archive that will not open says which of four things stopped it. Filed dcc: a document format with a total, inspectable read is what a DCC/IDE-class editor is built on, and both node canvases in this tree get it. ★★★THE GAP WAS THE READ RATHER THAN THE WRITE: a Document has derived serde since R1577, so saving one is a call -- and the node editor hand-rolled an envelope whose load answered false for FOUR different reasons (not JSON / wrong version / broken invariants / nothing stored) while the node lab had no save at all. The reference toolkit's state restore has exactly that shape, runs its usability check pass privately and hands the caller none of it. pinion_node_graph::Archive::read does that pass and RETURNS it: Unreadable names which of four, Opening::violations is Document::validate's own verdict, Dropped names what would not survive (a selection pointing at a node that is gone, a camera whose zoom would blank the canvas), and Opening::reason is the one sentence a screen shows. ★★★★★THE COMPANION IS PARSED INDEPENDENTLY OF THE DOCUMENT, which a front-to-back stream cannot do: an application whose own saved state changed shape still gets its graph back and is told what was left behind, where the reference answers false for the whole window. ★★★THE CLUSTER IS ONE A SELF-CENSUS CANNOT SEE: the reference publishes its own operation list and even measures its coverage of it, spec::OPERATIONS mirrors those thirty one-for-one and R1688 finished them -- and saving is not on that list while being in the reference, alongside a fourth self-meter asking whether every piece of state is carried or declared volatile. So spec::KEPT is that partition and the gate asks the stronger question: drive each operation, save, open on a screen that has just started, and a SAVED slot must read what it read after while a VOLATILE one must read the opening value. The reference's meter only asks whether a key is classified; a key can be classified as carried and still not come back. ★★THE DISCRIMINATING SET IS CHECKED TOO -- five of the thirty put their scope back to how it opened, so their two readings are equal to begin with and prove nothing about a round trip; every classified slot must therefore have at least one operation that genuinely moves it away from the opening reading. ★★THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED: the reference puts save/open/clear in the canvas toolbar and so does this, TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER 431 to 609 and MIN_W 1447 to 1625, with the number derived by the gate rather than by hand (the hand said 594, and two other gates failed alongside it). ★Violation gained a Display, the one error-shaped type in that crate without one and the one most likely to be put in front of a person.

the palette says how much of the option surface it can author, and every string on that surface has a shape or is named as having none. The behaviour reference publishes FOUR self-censuses; this tree already mirrored its operation table (R1677) and its save partition (R1689), and these are the other two. Filed dcc because the config form IS the property-grid family. ★★★NOTHING DECLARED WHAT THE THING BEING CONFIGURED ACCEPTS, so the two questions a person picking a configuration tool asks first were unanswerable here: a palette of eleven keys over a surface of eleven is finished and over a surface of forty is a start, and the two looked identical. `pinion_core::widgets::config_schema` is the declaration -- leaf paths with the shape each holds, validated where it is built, because a path cannot be a value and a section at once and a schema admitting both would make `document()` pick one silently. Over it, `reached_by` reports TWO numbers (sections 11/19, leaves 11/36) because one hides the other -- a tool can touch every section and reach a small fraction of the leaves, and the sections figure is a FOLD of the leaves figure rather than a second count, since two independently counted numbers over one catalogue can tell different stories -- and `strings` partitions the string half into word-set / has-a-shape / free, exclusive and total BY CONSTRUCTION because the class is read off the declared shape rather than kept in three lists beside it. Neither figure is written anywhere: both are recomputed from the palette every time they are asked, which is the only version of a coverage meter worth painting, and a test drops a field and reads the number to hold that. ★★★★★THE HALF THE REFERENCE DOES NOT HAVE IS THE HALF THAT FOUND THE DEFECT: a reach count answers "is the key offered" and stops, so it is blind to a key offered at a shape the target REFUSES -- the chip is there, the row is there, the typed value is accepted, and the node does not come up, with every count saying that key is covered. `Reach::mistyped` is that column, and this screen had exactly it: the node identifier is read by a parser and was typed as FREE TEXT for its whole life. The repair is not the row -- a row's shape now comes FROM the surface, so the palette cannot offer a key at a shape the target would refuse. ★★★★★AND THE SAME METER WAS FIRST WRITTEN WITH THE WRONG REACH RULE, WHICH A PROOF CAUGHT: it counted a catalogue key on the same root-to-leaf line, which is what a coverage figure over two path lists usually means and is wrong for THIS type -- a form field holds a scalar and `FieldType` has no arm for an object, so a key naming a SECTION composes a string where a subtree belongs. Proven through the form's own composition (the row yields a string at the section's path) and from the other side (the schema refuses to declare a path as both value and section). THREE OF THIS SCREEN'S SIX CHIPS DID EXACTLY THAT -- `timestamping`, `compression`, `plugins` -- and no coverage count could see it, because the key IS on the surface. A leaf is reached only when a catalogue key EQUALS it; the rest are reported as `unauthorable`, kept apart from `unknown` because the two take different repairs. ★★★★THE MIDDLE STRING CLASS NEEDED AN ARM AND `FieldType::Formatted` IS IT, over `TextFormat`: a small declarative grammar (characters with a class and a length, a bounded number, a word from a set, head-sep-tail, a repeated part, an alternation) with no domain in any arm -- an address of the scheme/host:port kind is a composition of three of them, so the next domain needs no new arm. `judge` answers THREE states, and past what a caret-level validator in a mature toolkit answers it says two things that kind of validator does not: `Unfinished` means "some continuation of this would be right", which is what lets a value be TYPED, and every refusal carries the shape as a sentence DERIVED from the declaration plus the byte offset the text first went wrong at. The gate over the third state is a property rather than an example -- every prefix of every acceptable text is never refused, walked over a corpus -- because typing is a walk through prefixes. And because the grammar is data, an agent can read what a field will accept before writing to it. ★★★★★ENFORCING A DECLARED SHAPE FOUND THREE BAD VALUES IN THE SCREEN'S OWN SEED DATA: three of the eight opening identifiers were written as role initials and two of those initials are outside the hexadecimal alphabet the identifier is read with. The fallback was worse than the seed -- every card the palette added opened holding the same unparseable value, so the defect was being PRODUCED once per added node. ★★★★AND THREE EXTRA PROBLEM LINES WERE ENOUGH TO REACH A SECOND DEFECT NOTHING HAD BEEN ABLE TO PRODUCE: the launch gate's panel sized itself from how many problems there are, which is unbounded, so it was placed above the top of the canvas and the pane-local conversion underflowed. It is bounded by the canvas now and COUNTS what it has no room for, because the verdict is derived from all of the problems and a silent truncation leaves a gate closed for reasons the screen is not showing. Driven at the floor window size, where the bound is reachable with a graph a test can build; the first draft guarded that assertion and would have passed on a panel that simply fitted. ★★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS WERE FINDINGS BEFORE THEY WERE COUNTERFACTUALS: breaking "a number under its minimum can still grow into range" changed NOTHING, because every `Number` this tree builds has min 0 and the branch was unreachable from the corpus -- a bounded number is in the corpus now, which is the fourth occurrence of the class [[debt-a-gate-that-only-sees-correct-code-is-unproven]] names. And the first form of the mistyped break did not COMPILE, which is not a counterfactual. ★★★★★AND ONE COUNTERFACTUAL PASSED, WHICH WAS A THIRD FINDING: replacing the DERIVED sections figure with an independently counted one left everything green, because the two agree on every palette whose keys are all leaves -- they diverge on exactly one shape, a key naming a section, and the test for that case asserted the leaf figure and not the section one. It asserts both now. That is the assertion-in-a-place-it-can-fail lesson met a third time inside one round. 16 counterfactuals: 13 caught in the sweep, the other 3 after the break was made compilable or the assertion it needed was written. ★★★THE KILLED FIRST SWEEP LEFT THE TREE MUTATED AND THE CHECK MISSED IT -- exactly the hazard the driver's own docs record -- and what hid it is that the mutation was behaviourally inert, so the second run's baseline was GREEN over a tree nobody intended. ★★LOOKING AT THE WINDOW RENAMED THE METER: the label said `fields`, sitting directly above a form of field rows whose count happened to equal the section count beside it, so its two plausible readings agreed by coincidence. ★AND THE REFERENCE-MATCH DEMO'S PRESS CENSUS LEARNED THAT A CONTROL BELOW A FOLD IS REACHABLE: it read a missing window rectangle as "painted where a pointer cannot reach", which was true only while every control happened to fit at the design size. It scrolls to the offset the screen publishes and presses there, and prints how many needed it. 3 crates green, 12 demos of this screen green.

the screen says all of itself: every addressable region has a voice in the accessibility tree or declares why it has none. Filed dcc rather than none -- R1581 set the precedent that an accessibility REPAIR is not a Phase B advance, and this is not one: the property grid's controls now announce the kind their SHAPE is (a boolean row was a text box to a screen reader, telling somebody to type into a toggle), every affordance inside a control has a voice, and that is property-grid depth on the axis R1604 judges by depth. ★★★★★THE QUESTION COULD NOT BE ASKED: a screen paints regions and publishes an a11y tree, built by different code, and nothing said whether they agree. Measured on the analyzer's first screen: 166 addressable regions painted, 30 of them announced (the tree held 35 nodes and five are virtual description regions, a distinction nothing had ever drawn), so 136 unclassified -- and every check was green, because a region with no node paints perfectly and answers every question about its rectangle. The three clusters that DID have one each had a round that asked for it; nothing had ever asked about the rest. ★★★★THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN (not read): a probe compiled against the reference toolkit at 6.11.1 answered 7 nodes for a window of six children, 4 with an EMPTY name -- a forgotten button, a decorative rule, a custom painted region and the window. The forgotten control and the ornament are the same answer there. Clearing every author-settable accessibility slot on the rule changed the tree by nothing; hiding it left the node and took the ink; a label bound to a field announced its text twice. It has the tree and no census of it. ★★★THE SUBSTRATE: pinion_core::voice -- Silence{kind,detail} with a Relay DERIVED per kind (no two share one), covers_subtree true for every kind but the layout box, independent of the ink; and a five-arm Voice of which THREE are different defects with different repairs. `dangling` -- quiet because another node says its name, where that node does not speak -- is the arm no set difference can produce, and it caught this round's own largest defect twice over. Published as scene/voice, joining the painted scene with the SAME producer scene/access runs; scene/access also grew the reason R1668 gave the node and this serializer never read. ★★TOTALITY ALONE IS WORTHLESS: a census is satisfiable by declaring everything silent, so spec::VOICES and spec::SILENCES pin the SPLIT, by population rather than by tag, and are driven in both directions. ★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED, both 'the corpus never reached the arm': flipping the boolean role was caught by nothing because this screen has five fields and not one boolean, and the replacement test then let a single-choice set announce as checkboxes because it checked NAMES and not KINDS. Repaired where the mapping lives, over every FieldType, with a bijection against what the painter laid out. 19 counterfactuals, 19 caught after those two repairs. 4 crates + 5 examples green, clippy green with four findings repaired rather than allowed, and the demo blast radius run against release binaries.

a voice is judged, not only counted: a node in the accessibility tree is not a voice, and the census stops accepting one as an answer. Filed catalog because the repairs land across the WIDGET CATALOG rather than on one screen -- a data grid's rows announced their drag-handle glyph, a todo list's items announced a ballot box, a code editor announced its fold chevron, eight scrub sliders and a switch announced their role and nothing, two grid corners and a tree container had no name, a tab panel announced its own identifier, and five document rows and seven list items announced nothing at all. ★★★★★MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE TREE, through 216 running applications: 5,427 addressable regions, 2,645 announced, 51 declared quiet, 2,695 unvoiced -- and the first run of the rules flagged 42 rows across 24 surfaces that were all green. THIRTY WERE DEFECTS AND TWELVE WERE THE RULES BEING WRONG, which is the finding rather than a caveat on it: ten grid cells whose emptiness is the DATA (the empty half of an optional column) and two live regions, which are announced when they change rather than navigated to and owe no rectangle. Each produced a rule rather than an exception -- AriaRole::name_required and Announcement::live. The thirty repaired, and re-measured at zero. ★★★★★THE RULES ARE NOISE WITHOUT OWEDNESS, and the floor proves it: a probe compiled against the reference toolkit at 6.11.1 and run offscreen answers 9 nodes for a window of six regions, EIGHT of which fail one of the three rules added here -- five with an empty name of which exactly ONE is a defect, one announcing its own object name, and one announcing a glyph the framework DERIVED from the button's visible text by construction. Nothing there separates a region that owes a reader a voice from one that does not; here the R1691 silences supply exactly that, so a flag is a defect rather than a suspicion. ★★★★THE VOCABULARY: NameFault (absent / address / wordless), each decidable from tag and name alone and each a real defect on this tree. The address rule requires the tag to be STRUCTURED, because three tags here equal their names and are RIGHT -- those screens paint that word as the visible label, which is WAI-ARIA's own rule. And AriaRole::name_required, an exhaustive match so a forty-third role cannot inherit an answer nobody chose, excuses only cell / gridcell / generic: ten cells of one grid are the empty half of an optional column, where a name would be an invention rather than a repair. ★★★THE PROMISE CHECKABLE ONLY FROM BELOW: `layout` says the children speak, and nothing asked. Voice::Hollow is that arm, expressed as Relay::unkept -- every relay mapped once to what a broken promise makes it, with the invariant that a relay is reachable exactly when its unkept form is a defect. ★★★THE GHOST EXEMPTION WAS ONE-DIRECTIONAL: it excused a node something POINTS AT and not one that points at painted ink. Eight of this tree's nine ghosts were exactly that shape and none was a defect; a third anchor is a live region, which owes no rectangle because it comes to the reader. ★★THE SECOND CONSUMER: scene/voice answered every binding since R1691 and one screen ever asked it. a screen is a tree a reader can walk: an announced role that promises members and holds none is a lie no per-node check can see. Filed modelview because the mechanism is WAI-ARIA's structural relation over tables, trees, grids and lists, its framework consumers are the data-view builders (grid_table_nodes, grouped_grid_access_nodes, listbox_option_nodes), and the forcing screen is a three-pane capture viewer whose grid, tree and byte grid are all Model/View shapes. ★★★THE QUESTION NO EXISTING CENSUS COULD ASK. R1691 asked whether every painted region has a voice; R1692 asked whether that voice says anything usable. Both are about ONE NODE AT A TIME, and neither can see a node that is perfect on its own terms and structurally a lie: a pane announcing role=table, named, with a rectangle a reader can land on, that holds no row. An assistive technology says "table" and there is nothing to move into. Measured on the reference analysis tool's screen B the day this started: 186 addressable regions, THREE announced nodes, two of which were exactly that. ★★★★★THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN, IS STRONGER ON ONE SIDE AND ABSENT ON THE OTHER. Two probes compiled against 6.11.1 and executed offscreen. A model-driven 16x7 item view answers 137 nodes, a table interface reporting sixteen rows and seven columns, and a cell lookup by row and column naming the cell and reporting its own row, column and column header -- which is why this round tags every cell rather than only its rows: tagging rows alone would have been strictly LESS navigable than the thing it is meant to beat. The same view with its model emptied answers the table role, a row count of zero, and NO DIAGNOSTIC; a tree with no items answers the same way. A two-column tree -- exactly screen B's decode pane -- announces a row as TWO SIBLING ITEMS, the value reporting itself expandable like the field it belongs to, leaf rows reporting themselves expanded while reporting they cannot expand, and no hierarchy at all. A custom-painted 72-cell pane answers ONE node, empty-named, with no children. So the floor derives a complete tree for the shapes it owns, nothing for the shapes it does not, and in neither case a verdict about the tree's FORM. ★★★★★EMPTINESS IS DECLARED, NOT INFERRED, AND THAT IS WHAT LETS THE GATE BE BUDGET ZERO. A collection with no members is a real state -- a filter that matched nothing, a capture with no messages -- and a rule refusing it would make that state unrepresentable. So the rule is the one R1691 applied to silence: an empty collection is well-formed WHEN IT SAYS IT IS EMPTY, in ARIA's own extent vocabulary (aria-rowcount / aria-colcount / aria-setsize of zero). "It is legitimately empty" stops being an exception a screen pleads and becomes a declaration the census checks. ★★★★MEASURE FIRST, THEN CHOOSE THE BUDGET. A sweep of all 216 answering surfaces found 12 carrying a violation (13 empty, 44 stray) -- small enough to close in the round that found it, which is the only reason the gate refuses at zero instead of becoming another ratchet. 200 would have forced a ratchet, and a ratchet records defects rather than refusing them. ★★★AND THE RULES WERE WRONG TWICE BEFORE THEY WERE RIGHT, both found by running them over the corpus rather than by reasoning: the first draft gave `radio` a required context and false-flagged a standalone one (WAI-ARIA requires radiogroup->radio and not the reverse -- copying one column of an asymmetric relation into the other INVENTS A RULE), and adding declares_empty took the count from 16 surfaces to 12. THE TWELVE WERE THREE CLASSES AND ONLY ONE WAS EXPECTED: three panels announced `list` and had never built a listitem (they paint prose -- and each had a perfectly good NAME the whole time, which is why a good name is not evidence of a right role); five had trees that stopped short (a header strip owning none of its five column headers and itself inside nothing -- the requirement chain is ARIA saying the tree ended two levels early; a calendar owning its seven headers and thirty-one days DIRECTLY, with no weeks in it, so the shape a sighted reader sees was not the shape a reader was given; a group header row with no cell; a command palette announcing a listbox and never one option); three lists open empty and did not say so. ★★★★THE 3RD-CONSUMER ANSWER WAS THE BUILDER, NOT THE CALL SITES: listbox_option_nodes and grid_table_nodes now state their container's extent, so the fourth consumer is right by construction instead of being repaired. ★★★★★TAGGING THE CELLS EXPOSED A PAINTER DEFECT NOBODY COULD HAVE ASKED ABOUT: at the declared floor, message 6's resource name was painted at ZERO WIDTH -- its two annotations are wider than the whole name column, and the column's floor was a number somebody picked. Same defect and same repair as the comment one level up already recorded (a floor somebody picks can be wrong about the thing it is a floor FOR), now derived at compile time from the widest annotation load the capture holds. A sighted reader had been losing that message's name and no check had ever asked whether the cell was painted, BECAUSE UNTIL THIS ROUND THE CELL HAD NO TAG TO ASK ABOUT. ★★★★★AND "IS INTERPRETED" IS STILL NOT "WORKS", AGAIN: this screen matched the chords `Down` and `Up`, which no key press produces -- the shell spells a named key the way the web platform does, and every other example in the tree matches ArrowDown. Its keyboard navigation had never worked from a keyboard, and every test that drove it passed because every test used the screen's own spelling: the test and the defect were the same mistake. The round that announced this list as a `grid` -- a composite widget whose contract IS that the arrows move the selection -- is what made anyone drive a real key. Class measured across all 225 examples: one instance, now zero. Screen B closes at 291 addressable regions, 266 announced, 25 declared quiet, 0 unclassified, 0 voice defects, 276 announced nodes, judged 276, 0 empty, 0 stray -- from 186 regions and 3 nodes. Its spec::Population also settled debt-a-voice-family-can-only-expand-from-a-table-the-spec-has by being the second consumer the debt said was the only possible evidence: it declares a PRODUCT of two tables, a RANGE from a scalar, and four families expanded by a predicate, with no new machinery -- what has to generalise is the expander, which was already a function.

a locked seat is heard, or it is not a locked seat. Filed modelview because the framework deliverable is the shared item-view grid builder, and because the tool DEMANDED this axis's re-judgment (round ledger 11 -> 14, +27%): re-audited, it HOLDS at 95, since all eight gaps R1563 named still stand and what this round closed was never counted. ★★★★★THE SCREEN'S SUBJECT WAS INAUDIBLE. Its section headings come back as list items indistinguishable in role from the entries (sixteen flat items, no grouping, and "thirteen entries, nine reserved" not derivable from anything announced), and the one slot that could carry a reason is free-form prose that on a toolbar action DEFAULTS TO THE ACTION'S OWN LABEL -- measured directly: every unlocked seat's description equals its name. ★★★★MEASURE FIRST, THEN CHOOSE THE BUDGET, again: over 215 answering surfaces there are 13 stated reasons and ELEVEN WERE UNHEARD, all on this one screen, so the gate's new half refuses at ZERO with an empty exception list instead of becoming a ratchet. WAI-ARIA counts it in aria-rowcount so it must be counted in aria-rowindex -- and grid_table_nodes stated a grid's EXTENT and gave no row or cell its COORDINATES AT ALL, which is below the floor on the dimension the floor is strongest on (its cell query answers the cell's name, its row, its column and its column header). The capture screen's copy numbered its data rows from one, leaving its header unplaced and its last row unreachable. The rule now lives once in the builder, with the row's WAI-ARIA name-from-contents beside it, and BOTH screens were converted onto the builder rather than corrected in place. ★★★THE REASON IS DECLARED ONCE: nothing in the screen's accessibility code restates a lock -- the row declares Unavailable on its layout style and the assembler relays what the cascade resolved -- and a unit test asserts the tree built in isolation carries NO reason at all, so the relay is what the demo proves end to end. ★★THE VOICE CENSUS FOUND ITS OWN as soon as the cells were tagged: the identifier map's unresolved timestamp is painted as an em dash, the typographic stand-in for a value nobody has, and announced as itself it is a punctuation mark with no word in it; it now announces its meaning. ★★★★★AND THE ENTRY CENSUS FOUND R1693's OWN RED: hello-lazy-tree failed the structural gate at boot with a tree holding no treeitem, which is not FORGOTTEN but WAITING -- aria-busy, read from the same predicate the status band already puts into words (R1693.1, committed separately, with a test that fails both ways). A second failure on that demo was proven PRE-EXISTING by running the pristine binary with the gate disabled and comparing the failure MESSAGE. ★★★AND THE THIRD-CONSUMER RULE FIRED: two screens had byte-identical `tagged_label` helpers and this round's table cells made three, so `pinion_widget_paint::run::text_run` is the lift -- holding two decisions in one place, that a run's layout rectangle IS its text rectangle (or every tag-keyed check reads a box the glyphs are not in) and that a run is transparent to the pointer (or it shadows the control it labels). Screen C closes at 193 regions, 190 announced, 3 declared quiet, 0 undecided, 0 voice defects, 159 nodes judged, 0 empty, 0 stray -- from 128 regions and 5 nodes. 14 of 14 counterfactuals CAUGHT, none passed; three were rewritten first because the break did not COMPILE, which tests nothing, and each was recast as a WRONG answer rather than an absent one.

arriving is not highlighting: a navigation rail that moves a string is not a rail that takes you anywhere, and nothing in this tree could tell the two apart. Filed catalog and the axis RE-JUDGED 98 -> 99, which the standing note above demanded be breadth rather than depth: the four absent widget kinds are three, because pinion_core::widgets::destination plus pinion_widget_paint::pages IS the paged container that list has named since R1554. The other three and the wheel hook are untouched, which is why it is one point. ★★★★★THE DEFECT, MEASURED BY DRIVING THE RUNNING APPLICATION THROUGH THE ROUTER BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. The analysis tool's dashboard offers seven destinations. Pressing Stream, Decode, Catalog or Settings moved `nav` -- the string the rail highlights ITSELF from, read by nothing else -- and left the painted scene at 193 TAGGED REGIONS BEFORE AND 193 AFTER, nothing added and nothing removed. The screen said Stream and showed the dashboard. On the sibling screen every seat answered "X is not this screen", INCLUDING the seat that screen already was (false) and the two declared unavailable with a stated reason (which got that sentence instead of their reason). And the two screens' rosters share TWO KEYS OUT OF SEVEN: one tool, two lists of what the tool contains. ★★★★★WHY EVERY GATE WAS GREEN THROUGH ALL OF IT: the existing check is assert_router_press_moves, which asserts a press MOVED THE STATE -- exactly what a screen that highlights a seat and shows nothing new does. Moved is not arrived, and the difference is a rectangle. ★★★★THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11.1 rather than read about: its paged container addresses a page by ORDINAL; setCurrentIndex returns void so an out-of-range ordinal is a silent no-op with no diagnostic; a DISABLED PAGE IS ARRIVED AT ANYWAY (currentIndex becomes 2 for a page that refuses); a destination that has no page yet cannot be expressed at all; a non-current page stays LIVE and, sent a press, a key and a wheel directly, counted all three -- so input scoping there is a guard the author repeats at every handler, which is precisely what the behaviour reference does (its wheel handler opens by testing that the active section is its own); and the container's accessible value is EMPTY, so no client can ask which page is showing, while a locked rail seat answers focusable, selectable with no unavailable state at all. ★★★★THE SUBSTRATE ANSWERS EACH ROW: the key is the address (an ordinal makes reordering the rail and changing where a press goes the same edit); navigate returns a typed Detour carrying the reason; a destination with no page is an ordinary roster entry whose Standing is Closed; the page that is not current is NEVER CONSTRUCTED, because view_page_region hands the builder only the destination it is at, so scoping is structural rather than remembered; and the region is a named `region` landmark publishing which destination arrived. The reason value is the framework's existing Unavailable rather than a second vocabulary -- one arm added to it, Elsewhere, because a product with more than one surface must be able to say BUILT, SHIPPING AND NOT HERE, and neither reserved (wait for a release that has already arrived) nor unsupported (give up on a feature one window away) means that. It derives its own Recourse::OpenElsewhere, which is the rule that module states for spending an arm: the reader's next action is its own. ★★★A SECOND PAGE, BECAUSE A PAGED REGION WITH ONE PAGE PROVES NOTHING ABOUT PAGING. The reference's own Settings section, reproduced: four switch rows in two groups with the reference's alternating opening values, two affordances booked for a later release, and a two-way appearance segment. Both new control shapes are CATALOGUE WIDGETS rather than hand-drawn -- the first draft painted a box with a word in it and the words sat flush against their left borders, measured by ink span (Import... inked at 683 in a box from 682), and the repair is view_button, which centres with flex. ★★★★★THE CENSUS LEARNED TO WALK MORE THAN ONE SCREEN, which is half of debt-the-voice-gate-judges-only-the-opening-screen and the half that was called unclosable because nothing enumerated the screens an application has. The rail's roster IS that enumeration: every VoiceSpec / SILENCES / LOCKED row now says which destination owns it, the gates drive each open destination and compare in BOTH directions, and a page added without a row fails rather than escaping. Locked regions on this screen went 11 -> 16 as a direct consequence. ★★★★★16 COUNTERFACTUALS, 15 CAUGHT AND THE ONE THAT PASSED IS THE FINDING: emitting the settings page's accessibility nodes while the dashboard is showing left every check green, because they all read the PAINTED scene and a tree can announce what nothing paints. The demo's boot census caught it as four ghosts -- the right answer arriving one build later and only for the destination the application happens to open at -- so the law is now asked of the tree too, in-process, per destination. Two more findings arrived as ordinary failures: the region swallowed every press on its page until pointer transparency became structural in the substrate (the screen's own R1649 gate went red on the first run), and a `part_of` silence pointing at PROSE instead of a tag produced seven dangling rows. Also repaired, this round's defect in miniature: the Add Widget button moved the rail's highlight to a destination the window had not taken anyone to. 4 crates green (317 a11y, 3512 core, 886 widget-paint, 52 shell), 4 analyzer demos green, and the settings page was LOOKED AT -- which is what found the left-flush labels that no value check on this screen could report.

the screen has a keyboard. Declared `none`: this is a STOP-THE-LINE REPAYMENT of the red R1695's push inherited, plus the local gate that should have caught it and did not exist, and no Phase B capability moved -- the axis the repair lands on is accessibility, and R1581 set the precedent that an accessibility repair is not an advance. ★★★★★WHAT WAS RED, AND WHY THE ROUND THAT CAUSED IT COULD NOT SEE IT: two demos, one cause -- `hello-analyzer-shell` presents an interactive ARIA role and `focus/next` from cold answered NOTHING. It announces a navigation landmark of links, two toolbars, a list of items, four tabs, a textbox and thirty-nine buttons, and a keyboard reached none of them. R1694 is what put it there: an interactive role is what enrols a binding in `r1570.1`'s DERIVED population, so the screen joined the gate the moment it started declaring -- and both gates that walk it are python demos that run only in CI. The sibling screen learned the identical lesson at R1693 from the identical pair, which is the part worth keeping: a round that gives a screen its first accessibility tree acquires two gates it has never run. ★★★★THE REPAIR IS THE WAI-ARIA COMPOSITE PATTERN, the shape the sibling already holds: one stop per composite -- application bar, rail, layout bar, board, palette -- rather than one per control, plus the Settings page's switches and appearance segment, which are not inside a composite and declare their own stop through the catalogue widgets. The ring is `spec::FOCUS_RING`, a DECLARATION the paint reads rather than five independent decisions, and each row also says WHAT the stop holds, which is the part a tag cannot carry: an agent reading `focus_ring` off the wire learns that landing on the rail puts it among the tool's destinations rather than on one of them. ★★★★★THE ORDER IS THE PAINT ORDER AND THAT IS RATIFIED, NOT MISSING. The ring starts at the page, because the page must be painted UNDER the chrome, which is not the order a reader would choose. §5.39's own alternatives REJECT a manual tab index -- imitating HTML's tabindex violates the declarative spirit of a view function, automatic traversal is canonical -- so this was NOT worked around. Measured against the floor by building a probe and running it: `setTabOrder(bar,rail)` reorders the chain while the geometry stays put (page y=11, bar y=43, rail y=75 unchanged), so on this dimension the floor is above us, while its API is a static pairwise mutation with no way to ASK a widget its rank where this project publishes the whole enumeration -- each side holds half. Filed as a SPEC ROUND with the argument it has to weigh: "tree order is canonical" is a claim about an order the author CHOSE, and z-order takes that choice away from a screen whose chrome is painted over its page. The debt also records the alternative that needs no tab index at all -- give chrome a layer so child order stops carrying z-order -- and warns against the consumer-side "fix", which puts the chrome underneath the page. ★★★THE LIFT: R1693 wrote a four-line free function to make a painted region a Tab stop and this round needed a verbatim copy on the second screen, which is the exact trigger `Scene::silenced` was lifted on in that same round. It is `Scene::with_focusable` now and the free function is gone. ★★★★AND THE SIBLING SCREEN GAINS THE GATE IT NEVER HAD: a counterfactual reverting the lifted builder left EVERY test in `hello-packet-view` green while that screen lost its whole keyboard -- R1693 added its ring and left it verified only by the slow tree-wide demos. Both screens now assert their own ring in-process, derived from their own specification tables. ★★★THE GATE'S OWN HALF-VACUITY IS CLOSED EXPLICITLY: the paint reads the ring table, so "every declared stop is focusable" compares the table with itself, which R1669's rule says is not a check. What the table cannot produce is a stop it never named, so the enumerated set is closed against the table plus the catalogue widgets -- and the ORDER comparison is discriminating on its own, because paint order is not derived from the table. 5 counterfactuals, 4 caught, and the one that PASSED is a finding: flipping the booked affordance's `focusable` to true changed nothing in the Rust gate OR in the demo's negative control, because the row declares Unavailable and R1554's enumeration returns at a disabled region before reading any child's flag. Nothing was missing -- that rule is tested where it lives -- but a comment was claiming credit for a guarantee it does not provide, and now says which one is load-bearing. Both red gates re-run here against release binaries: r1570.1 151 assertions, r1518 529 assertions over 96 stops in 96 bindings. Five screenshots, one per stop, confirm the overlay ring draws correctly including on the two edge panels where a clipped ring would have been the obvious failure. What this round did NOT do is stated: arrow roving WITHIN each composite, which both analyzer screens lack equally, so it is one shared axis rather than a divergence.

a torn-off panel can be moved, and the dashboard declares its operations. Filed dcc because a floating panel a person moves, sizes and raises is a DCC/IDE-class capability, and because the thing that let its absence survive -- a screen with no operations table -- is now closed on the highest-leverage axis. ★★★★★THE DEFECT WAS REPORTED BY A PERSON USING THE TOOL. They tore a card off the board into a floating panel, tried to drag it, and asked whether it being nailed in place was intended. It was not: the press arm that would have started the gesture read `Hit::Float(_) | Hit::Nothing => {}` -- a detached panel folded in with hitting nothing at all -- and nothing anywhere opened a drag for one. EVERY GATE ON THAT SCREEN WAS GREEN AND EACH WAS RIGHT ABOUT ITS OWN QUESTION: the panel is painted, hit-testable, inside its own rectangle, named, and announced with its reason for being inert. None of them asks whether GRABBING IT MOVES IT, and none of them could, because the screen had no table saying it should. ★★★★THE SHAPE MOVED INTO THE FRAMEWORK RATHER THAN BEING COPIED. The sibling screen has had an operations table since R1677 and it caught this class three times there; a second hand-rolled copy is exactly debt-a-shape-two-screens-hand-roll-is-a-substrate-hole-nobody-censuses. So `pinion_core::operation::Operation` holds the columns (name / verb / gesture / witness / needs) and the checks a reader of the table alone can run -- faults() for a precondition naming nothing, a duplicate name, a row with no witness, an absent row carrying a precondition; in_order() for the order the preconditions impose, which a driver would otherwise encode a second and silently different time. Screen A adopts it by re-export with zero row edits. ★★★★★THE BEHAVIOUR IS THE REFERENCE'S, READ OUT OF ITS SOURCE: a panel opens 520x380 with a stacking number from a monotonic counter; grabbing it RAISES IT FIRST and then moves it by the pointer's delta; its corner sizes it and clamps at 320x220. The three are ONE GESTURE -- the drag calls the raise -- so building one alone leaves the other two in the wrong place. ★★★★TWO STRUCTURES FOLLOW FROM THE PIXEL PLANE NOT BEING THE BOARD'S. A card is dragged between cells and PREVIEWS where it would land, because the board reflows under the finger; a panel is dragged in pixels and moves as the pointer moves, because it lands where it is put. So the gesture in flight is its own type rather than an arm added to the card drag, whose fields are a cell coordinate and a snap target. And stacking becomes an explicit `z` rather than the roster's order read backwards: that order is the same answer ONLY WHILE NOTHING REORDERS THE PANELS, and a raise is exactly a reorder. ★★★★★THE GATE FOUND A SECOND DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, before the demo existed: a card maximised with the mouse had NO WAY BACK WITH THE MOUSE. The header control called `maximize` again, which refuses with "a card is already maximised; restore first", so the only ways back were Escape and the wire. It toggles now and paints a restore mark when it will -- a control that toggles without changing its mark tells a person the same thing in both states. The two WIRE verbs stay separate and precise, because an agent asking for a specific outcome should not get a toggle, and the demo asserts that refusal survives. ★★★★THE WITNESS HAD TO EXIST BEFORE THE OPERATION COULD BE TESTED: `floating` was a roster of ids and published no geometry, so a moved panel was invisible to every reader that is not a screenshot. That is why the defect survived -- the operation had no witness a test could name, so no test could name it. `floats` publishes each panel's x/y/w/h/z front to back, and every row's witness is read THROUGH the introspection surface rather than off a field, so "changed" means changed where a client can see it. ★★★★★10 OF 10 COUNTERFACTUALS CAUGHT -- but the first run was 3 CAUGHT, 2 PASSED and 3 BROKEN, and both halves are the finding. The three BROKEN did not compile, which tests nothing (the fourth time this class has been walked into): removing the only call site of a helper makes it dead code under -D warnings, so each was recast as a WRONG answer rather than an absent one -- grab a panel named "nothing", carry to where the grab opened, raise a name that is not a panel. The two that PASSED became gates: nothing checked that a point BOTH panels cover reaches the RAISED one after a raise has changed the order (every earlier assertion was satisfied by the pre-R1697 roster order, because the raised panel was also the one that order reached first), and nothing checked that a press which moved nothing does not announce a move -- the lie R1695 took out of the rail, coming back on a panel because a click on one opens a grab that then carries nothing. ★★★★AND THE ROUND WAS LOOKED AT, which found a defect no value check on this screen can report: the detach toast paints U+2192 and the face has no glyph for it, so a person reads "Decode Inspector [box] detached window". Not a pipeline fault -- U+00B7, U+2026, U+2014 and U+2212 all render in the same screenshot -- but a cmap gap with no second face to fall back to, because the shaper is called with a one-element stack. NOT papered over by swapping the character, which would be a workaround; registered with the measurement and with the gate that is already buildable from the framework's own cmap query. Verification: 3 crates green (core 3522, analyzer 57, node lab 83), clippy green, 5 demos green including a new 39-assertion integration test driven through a real window, and eight photographs of the panel being detached, moved, sized past its floor, stacked and raised.

a composite has a cursor inside it -- and the dashboard's keyboard reaches it from a keyboard at all. Filed catalog because what this adds is INTERACTION rather than a widget: the framework had no vocabulary for what a composite's arrows do, so every consumer invented one. The axis COMPLETION HOLDS AT 99 and that is deliberate -- none of its three named absent widget kinds moved and the wheel hook still has two implementors -- but the round is depth on the half of that axis's name that is not the catalog. ★★★★★WAI-ARIA'S COMPOSITE PATTERN IS TWO HALVES AND ONLY ONE WAS BUILT. R1693 and R1696 gave the two analysis screens one Tab stop per composite; nobody built the second, where an arrow moves a cursor between the members and the composite publishes where it rests. Measured by driving both running applications: eleven Tab stops, four arrow keys each, FORTY-FOUR PRESSES THAT MOVED NOTHING, and an active descendant that was `None` at every one. ★★★★★MEASURING IT FOUND SOMETHING WORSE UNDERNEATH. The dashboard's keymap of twelve chords was reachable ONLY THROUGH THE WIRE: `invoke("key", "ArrowRight")` moved the board and a real key press moved nothing, because the screen implemented no `apply_key` hook at all. Census over 225 examples: 172 bindings implement that hook and 135 read its `focused` argument; this screen implemented it ZERO times. Every test that drove its keyboard passed for exactly the reason R1693's did on the sibling -- the test and the defect were the same mistake, because every test used the channel that worked. And the sibling, whose keys did arrive, dropped `focused`: at ALL SIX of its stops -- the three filter chips, the decode tree and the byte grid included -- ArrowDown moved the MESSAGE LIST. ★★★★THE POLICY IS DECLARED RATHER THAN FIXED, because every composite answers differently and a framework that answers once answers wrongly for most of its consumers. `RovingSpec` names three (which arrows, what happens at the ends, whether arriving chooses) and settles a fourth for everybody: the cursor rests on a member that REFUSES, because a screen whose subject is that its locked seats are heard cannot use a cursor that hides them. what is drawn is what is pressed. Filed dcc because the surfaces repaired are the DCC/IDE-class ones -- a node-graph canvas with host frames, a decode grid, a dockable board -- and because the guarantee added is specifically about SELF-PAINTING surfaces, which is the architecture a node editor and an advanced data grid use in this framework. The axis COMPLETION HOLDS AT 88, re-judged rather than assumed: none of R1604's named gaps moved (the ~7 editor gestures, execution semantics and the two node-graph models are all untouched), and what moved instead is that the gestures this axis is ALREADY credited with are true at window sizes other than the one they were designed at. That is a soundness repair on existing credit rather than an addition to it, and saying so is what the tool asks for. *****THE DEFECT WAS REPORTED BY A PERSON, TWICE, AND MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. "R-01 will not press." "The row under the timestamping field does not respond." Both about a maximised window, both green in every gate. Driving the capture viewer through a real shell at 2494x1011 and asking it, at the centre of each rectangle it had just painted, what is here: of the 166 painted rectangles that MOVED under the resize, 166 answered NOTHING. Agreement zero. The paint reflowed to the live window and the hit test went on resolving against the size the screen was designed at. *****WHY NO GATE COULD SEE IT, AND BOTH REASONS ARE STRUCTURAL. The in-process sweeps paint and hit-test inside ONE owner scope, where both halves resolve the size hook and therefore CANNOT disagree -- the size axis is void by construction there. And the framework's own pointer guarantee covers the REGISTERED widgets: 2 #7 makes a pinion screen one External so an agent can query it, so on that screen scene/pointer_reach vouched for 1 OF 291 painted rectangles and the other 290 were on the screen's honour. ****THREE SCREENS SPELLED ONE QUESTION THREE WAYS AND ONE WAS WRONG. Asked off a view scope, the node lab read the framework's record (correct, R1684.4), the shell read a Signal on its own state through a weak handle (correct, R1671), the capture viewer read the design constant. So the POLICY moved into pinion_core::external::layout_size: the tracked viewport read inside a view (the window is the live fact there and the surface's own rectangle is not, because it comes out of the layout the view is feeding), the recorded surface rectangle outside one, the caller's floor honoured in both, the design size only for a surface nothing has painted. A policy re-derived per consumer has as many versions as consumers; this one had three and one defect. Its stated limit is written down rather than left implicit: a surface that does not fill its window gets the window from the in-view branch, and nothing can do better during its own view. ****THE REPAYMENT DID NOT HAVE TO BE ARGUED, IT STOPPED COMPILING. The shell's scope-free weak handle existed for exactly one reason; with layout_size answering in both places -D dead-code named it on the first build after the switch. It is gone, and so is the size copy on that screen's state that it reached, and the in-process sweep now publishes its size through the FRAMEWORK's channel instead of through a signal only that screen's own sweep could drive. *****THE SUBSTRATE IS THE MISSING QUESTION, ASKED TWICE. External::target_at says what a press at a point addresses; External::target_of_tag says what the thing painted under a tag addresses; both answer in the surface's own vocabulary, the one its wire already uses. scene/pointer_target asks both for every painted rectangle and holds the pair against the paint, which is the arbiter. TWO questions rather than one because a single "what tag is here" would need a hand-written inverse from the vocabulary back to the tags, and an inverse written by hand drifts from what it inverts -- R1699 met exactly that and wrote its gate before its function. PointerTarget has three arms and Unanswered is NOT Nothing: a surface that does not resolve presses is not one that resolved every press to nothing, and collapsing them would let a screen nobody checked read as a screen that checked out. The verdicts are pointer_reach's vocabulary one level down -- deliverable, handle, covering, inert, unreachable -- and only unreachable fails, because only it has no benign reading. *****THE GATE'S FIRST RUN REFUTED THE GATE. Its first rule asked whether a rectangle's CENTRE addresses it, and it reported the node lab's two host frames as defects. They are not: a group paints one rectangle around its members and is gripped by its tab strip, deliberately, because a group that took presses over its own members would make a card undraggable the moment it joined one. So the question became "somewhere inside", probed at nine points -- the centre first, then four edge midpoints and four inset corners, which is what reaches a strip a proportional grid would step over -- and a rectangle addressable at NONE of the nine is the failure. *****10 OF 10 COUNTERFACTUALS over two plans with two gates, AND THE TWO THAT PASSED FIRST ARE BOTH FINDINGS. Falsifying the RECORDED surface height changed nothing anywhere, because none of these three screens has an addressable rectangle positioned by the window's HEIGHT -- the vertical axis of the size question had no consumer to disagree through, while announce_external_sizes states that very invariant in its own comment and nothing read it; the report now publishes painted_size beside announced and the resize helper asserts they agree. And making the by-name answer name a NEIGHBOURING tag also passed, because a rectangle that stops being answered for by name becomes `covering`, which is a legitimate verdict (a label over the row it labels): the collapse was published as a number and nothing read the number, so a committed coverage floor per screen now fails a screen that quietly stops vouching for two thirds of itself. ****THE INTEGRATION TEST WAS WRONG TWICE MORE BY ASSUMING INSTEAD OF ASKING. It allowed a pane below the layout floor to be painted narrower "because the window clips" -- measured, a painted rectangle is the LAYOUT's and is cut only by the scroll viewports above it, so the allowance would have accepted a pane that had genuinely shrunk. And it wrote 1440x900 down as the design size; the node lab opens at 1625x900, so the constant was resizing that screen below its own floor and reporting it vouching for 54 rectangles where it vouches for 61. Each screen's design size is ASKED FOR now. ****THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN OFFSCREEN AT 6.11.1 RATHER THAN READ ABOUT. A widget's own size answers live inside a press handler there (1200x700 after a resize), which is the property layout_size had to match and does. None of the rest exists: a self-painting widget's eight painted marks are INVISIBLE to the framework's point lookup, which answers null; the scene-graph point lookup trusts an item's DECLARED shape and finds nothing where a paint drew outside it; and no member enumerates what a widget painted at all, because the only framework-held record of a paint there is pixels, which carry no identity. Introspection-from-paint is what makes the comparison possible here. ****AND THE ROUND WAS LOOKED AT, which found what no value check reports: the node lab's gesture strip was a flat 470px and read "... drag a pin = author a li..." with sixteen hundred pixels of empty canvas beside it. It is the size of its own sentence now, bounded by a third caller for the launch panel's left edge -- and the text-smear gate refused the first repair on its next boot because the full-width strip painted over that panel, which is the bound the constant had been providing by accident. VERIFICATION: 5 crates green (core 3548, rpc 1246 with 4 new, node lab 83, capture viewer 42, shell 66), harness suite 36 cases / 103 assertions with three new negative controls, a new integration test of 33 named checks over three screens x four window sizes, and -- because a new BOOT gate's blast radius is every demo while a full sweep is not judgeable on this host -- 25 further screens booted under it directly, 25 of 25 green with every surface `unanswered` and defects 0. Nine photographs. What this leaves is numbers rather than silence: the shell answers by name for 28 of its 192 painted rectangles and leaves 152 honest `covering`, published on every boot and floored in the test.

a title bar takes two clicks. Filed dcc because an in-application window a person maximises by double-clicking its header is a DCC/IDE-class capability -- the same axis R1697 filed a torn-off panel under -- and because the framework half lands on the client-side window chrome, which is what a tool that draws its own frame needs. The axis COMPLETION HOLDS AT 88, re-judged rather than assumed: none of R1604's named gaps moved. *****THE ASK WAS A QUESTION AND THE ANSWER WAS MEASURED. "Shouldn't double-clicking a window toggle minimise and maximise?" It should -- maximise and restore, which is what the convention actually is -- and nothing here did it. Driven through a real shell with a working positive control: pressing the dashboard card's maximize CONTROL took `maximized` from '' to 'decode#1' and back, so the witness moves; double-clicking the same card's header left it at ''. ****THE FIRST MEASUREMENT MEASURED NOTHING, and saying so is the point: it watched the window chrome's painted GLYPHS, which are paths rather than text runs, so the witness came back empty at rest and after every gesture -- "nothing happened" read off a list that could not have said anything else. Third occurrence of that class in one session, met while investigating it. ****THE CANON CANNOT SETTLE THIS AND SAYS SO: the behaviour reference is a browser prototype with no window chrome, ZERO double-click handlers in 194,828 bytes of application script, measured by extracting it. That absence is an artifact of the medium rather than a design decision, so the debt's own rule applies and this is filed as FLOOR PARITY. ****THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN OFFSCREEN AT 6.11.1 RATHER THAN READ ABOUT: an in-application sub-window's title-bar double-click takes it from 300x200 to its parent's full 900x600 (maximised 0 -> 1); a docking panel's takes it from docked to floating; and a frameless top-level is left ENTIRELY to its application, with no framework member that maps the gesture -- which is exactly what a client-side chrome is. *****TWO PLACES NEEDED IT AND ONLY ONE WAS THE SCREEN'S FAULT. The screen's half: the router has synthesised a `DoubleClick` send event since R664 and the dashboard REFUSED it as "not a pointer event"; it decodes it now through the same `act` entry the header button takes, refusal and all, so a card whose header does not offer maximise refuses the gesture BY NAME. The framework's half: a press on client-side chrome is consumed by the shell and returns before the widget router runs -- deliberately, because a title bar is not a widget -- so the router's double-click detector never sees one and a title bar could not tell a second click from a first. `chrome_press_intent(tag, count)` answers it in the crate that owns the tags, with the count as an ARGUMENT rather than a second function so the shell cannot grow a private rule beside it. *****AND THE RULE BECAME A TYPE, BECAUSE THERE ARE TWO DETECTORS NOW. `RawPointerButton::click_count`'s doc promised since R1422 that the raw stream and the send wire "share the framework double-click time + distance window so the two rules cannot drift" -- a guarantee resting on a comment and two literals in one file, which held while there was one detector. `pinion_core::input::DoubleClickWindow` is that promise as a value: the router keeps one per pointer, the chrome keeps one per window, the thresholds have one definition, and the file's three readers cite it. *****DRIVING IT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT THE DEBT FILE HAD PREDICTED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT. A grip press OPENS A BOARD DRAG, so a double-click is press/release/press/release over a card that maximises in the middle of it -- and the trailing release committed a move aimed at the board that existed BEFORE the card grew. Measured: "Decode Inspector moved, displacing Message Stream, Identifier Map, Search & Filter", and a second double-click never came back to the arrangement the screen opened with. A double-click SUPERSEDES the gesture its second press opened. *****AND A THIRD, PRE-EXISTING, WHICH IS R1697's OWN RULE ON THE ARM BESIDE THE ONE IT FIXED. R1697 wrote "nothing checked that a press which moved nothing does not announce a move" and built the guard for a detached panel; a card on the board told the same lie -- a single click on a header reported "Decode Inspector moved" with the layout byte-identical -- and worse, `move_to` is a real edit, so a click carrying nothing could still reflow the board and displace three cards. The guard compares against where the tile IS rather than a remembered origin, because a maximise between the press and the release moves it without the drag having carried it. ****AND THE ROUND WAS LOOKED AT, TWICE, WHICH IS WHERE THE LAST TWO REPAIRS CAME FROM. The gesture strip did not name the new gesture -- a capability built and not announced, the mirror of one announced and not built, and this screen has been on both sides of that. Adding it pushed the strip past its band, so the band is derived from the panel beside it now rather than being a flat 470; measured, the room at the design width IS 470, so the derivation reproduced the constant and the SENTENCE had to give. `Enter max` left, by the same rule that let the new item in: a double-click has NO AFFORDANCE, while Enter duplicates a button that is on screen and a keymap panel that names it in full. Ink 468 -> 427 in a 470 band, measured before and after. *****7 OF 7 COUNTERFACTUALS, and the one rewritten is the class this project has now recorded five times: "delete the call site" made the helper dead code under -D warnings and tested NOTHING, so it became a WRONG answer instead -- resolve the gesture at the window's corner rather than under the pointer. *****STOP-THE-LINE, ATTRIBUTED RATHER THAN RERUN: one pinion-shell test went red on the build host on the round's last run, on its own self-validating control (74 != 74). It PASSED on that same host fifteen minutes earlier with that crate's inputs unchanged, and passes on this one -- so what moved is which face the system font enumeration resolved, and that is an INPUT to a control asserting "our fixture measures differently from the host's sans-serif". The test's own comment predicted this failure and forbids weakening it; the honest repair (pin the off-path fontconfig) cannot be verified from a host where it does not reproduce, so it is registered with the measurement rather than blind-fixed. Verification: 5 crates green locally, 2 new in-process tests driven through `invoke` (the door the router's events come in by, with the press point read out of the PAINTED scene after the first draft computed it and aimed at the application bar), a new real-window demo with a positive control and two negative ones over all four card headers, and three photographs.

Declared `none`: a dependency pin, no Phase B capability moved -- the same declaration R1635's bump made. ****THE TRIPLE PIN MOVED TOGETHER, which is the half this project has previously left behind: the submodule gitlink, BOTH `rev =` sites in the workspace manifest, and the lockfile. `git submodule update` moves only the worktree, so the gitlink needs its own `git add`. pin_sync reports `manifest = lock = vendor/sce`. ****WHAT ACTUALLY REACHES US, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Of the forty-three commits the bulk are the ECMAScript datamodel -- its standard library, its parser, its type inference from a <data> value -- and all fourteen of our documents declare datamodel="null", so none of it is on our path; two more refuse native cpp:/kt: conditions on backends that cannot lower them, and we emit Rust. What does reach us is the Rust emit: state_machine.rs 65 lines, entry_exit_actions.rs 47, module_index.rs 38, conflict_resolution.rs 20, send.rs 14, plus the shared state_machine.jinja2 72 and process_transition.jinja2 36. Every one of our documents regenerates. *****AND THE ONE REAL SEMANTICS COMMIT HAS NO SHAPE TO ACT ON HERE. 123e7fdba1 -- "give a state on the way to a target no default child", W3C SCXML 3.3 -- changes what happens when a transition targets a deep descendant through a compound ancestor. Measured by PARSING all fourteen documents plus the shared template with an XML parser rather than reading them: EVERY CHART IS DEPTH 1, flat sibling states under the root, and there is not one <parallel> in the tree. There is no "state on the way to a target" here because every target is a direct child of the root. That cuts both ways and both halves are stated: the bump is low-risk for us, AND our corpus gives the fix no exercise, so confidence in it is upstream's rather than ours. ****PROVED BY COMPILING AND DRIVING, the standing rule R1686.1 wrote after a bump changed what our documents MEANT and only a compile could tell. The build log carries the new revision three times; pinion-core 3551, pinion-runtime 567 and pinion-forge green; and eleven widgets whose interaction IS a statechart were driven through a real shell -- button, checkbox, toggle, disclosure, slider, text field, radio group, list box, key sequence, colour picker, dock panel -- every one transitioning, each pressed at a point read out of the framework's own scene/pointer_reach rather than written down. *****THE SLIDER NEEDED A SECOND MEASUREMENT AND THE FIRST ONE WAS MY WITNESS FAILING, not the widget. A frame signature over tagged rectangles cannot see a slider move, because its thumb is untagged geometry inside the widget's own rect, so "painted the same throughout" said nothing at all about it. Asked through the widget's own published state instead: Idle -> Hover, and value 0.150 / 0.850 / 0.500 for presses at 15% / 85% / 50%, tracking the press exactly. Third occurrence this session of a witness that cannot move reading like a failure. ****INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT A TEST FAILURE, and worth writing down because the message misdirects: the first remote run refused because the build host still held files the old submodule revision had and the new one does not -- the transfer adds and never deletes -- and it reports "the remote working tree differs from this one", which reads like a fact about the far side when what moved was here.
