The worktree tool grows the half it was missing: a way BACK (`land`), and a round number that is CLAIMED rather than derived. Declared `none` — this is process tooling and moves no Phase B axis; the tally counts artifacts and a script that carries files between trees creates none, which is exactly the R1526 case that row file exists for. WHAT WAS WRONG: `add` / `list` / `remove` meant the FRONT half of a round had a tool and THE HANDOFF BETWEEN THE HALVES HAD NONE. R1757 landed by hand and every step of it is the argument: the patch was exported, `git apply` was tried, then a `cp` loop, and the three questions that make any of that legitimate — do the two trees agree on HEAD, does my file set collide with what the main tree already holds uncommitted, did the worktree touch a main-tree-only path — were answered by hand with `comm -12` and eyes. TWO OF THOSE THREE PROTECT WORK THAT IS NOT MINE, and a check made by hand is a check that will one day not be made; the day it is not made the loss is silent, because a `cp` over another session's uncommitted file leaves no diff to review and nothing to recover from. `land` asks all three and REFUSES. It never merges, never commits, never stages: it copies, verifies with `cmp` that the bytes arrived, and prints the exact `git add` line plus what the main tree still owes (ledger entry, TSV row, gates re-run) — closure stays serial because the ledger is why it is serial. IT REFUSES WHAT IT CANNOT EXPRESS, BY NAME: a delete, a rename, a submodule gitlink move, and the two ledger paths each get their own verdict rather than a guess. A delete could have been replayed with `rm` and a rename with two more copies, and both are destructive actions derived from a two-character status parse — this file's own history says what that is worth, since the first `classify_submodule_status` guessed and printed "verified" on a fatal git error. ROUND NUMBERS ARE NOW CLAIMED: `git log` cannot see a round that has not committed, so two sessions starting the same afternoon derive the same next number, and on 2026-08-21 R1757 and R1758 were BOTH BEGUN AS "R1757" — the collision surfacing only because one session happened to read the other's memory file, after which 85 sites were renumbered. `add` claims one past both git's newest and every live claim, into the state directory it already keeps, and `list` shows every claim; two `add`s now yield R1759 and R1760, demonstrated rather than argued. THE REMOTE BUILD LANE IS UNREACHABLE FROM A WORKTREE AND IS NOT FIXED HERE: `bx` resolves its repo root from the current directory with no override, so with the shell pinned to the main tree it rsyncs the MAIN tree to a build host and runs the worktree's `--manifest-path` against a directory that is not there (exit 101 in 17s, and its "trees agree" line is true about the wrong tree). R1757 therefore ran all eighteen builds `--local` while pc2 held 21 free cores of 32 and this host was 21GB into swap. That fix belongs to `~/.claude/remote-build`, its own repository and machine-wide across 51 projects, so from here it is a handoff (`docs/handoff-bx-root-flag.md`) plus the pinion-side half — `add` prints a paste-ready `wtb` function and says in the same breath that it forces local execution and is a stopgap. ★WRITING THAT HANDOFF BROKE THE TARGET REPOSITORY FOR A MINUTE, recorded rather than tidied away: the first draft was written INTO `~/.claude/remote-build` on the sprag precedent that a handoff may land in another repo's gitignored area — it is not gitignored there, and that repository's own `.gitignore` explains in a comment why an untracked file is not free, since `bx` includes `git status --porcelain` in the tree fingerprint it compares across hosts, so ONE stray path makes the two sides disagree forever and every gate that sends that repository refuses (it had already cost four days of red tests on a `bin/bx.bak-*`). The file was removed, the repository restored, and the handoff lives in pinion where the requirement originates. VERIFIED: selftest PASS (25 new assertions, inside the `pre-push` gate that already ran this tool's selftest at line 97), `shellcheck` clean, `tools/test_hooks.sh` 129/0, counterfactuals 6/6 CAUGHT. ★CF-1 PASSED ON THE FIRST RUN AND THAT WAS THE FINDING: the two ledger entries take DIFFERENT arms — one a directory, one an exact path — and the suite asserted only the exact-path sibling, so breaking the directory arm left it green; two assertions added and CF-1 then CAUGHT. Over-refusal is the quiet direction, since `land` would have refused a legitimate file with an official-looking reason. DRIVEN FOR REAL as well, because pure helpers cannot show that the command wires them up: two worktrees created, a ledger path refused by name, an overlapping path refused WITH THE MAIN TREE'S COPY VERIFIED INTACT AFTERWARDS, the clean case landing one file and printing its `git add`, and a HEAD-mismatched worktree refused with both hashes named. ★That live run found what the selftest could not — the refusal banner used BACKTICKS inside a double-quoted bash string, so it command-substituted and printed `land: command not found` above the refusal it was announcing; fixed, with a self-grep confirming no other double-quoted backtick in the file. NOT RE-RUN and stated: the Rust suites, since this round changes one bash script and adds one markdown file and touches no crate.

R1757's published counter free-ran on the clock, CI caught it, and the repair is that a delivery's NUMBER is claimed by a keystroke rather than handed out at the door. Declared `none`: this repays a defect this campaign introduced, and R1628's rule is that repayment restores credit rather than adding it — the §7 `api` axis was rejected by R1757 for widening undeclared surface, and fixing what that surface MEANS does not change the judgment. WHAT WAS BROKEN: R1757 published `key_delivery.opened` and told agents to read it either side of a burst, the difference being how many deliveries the request opened, and THAT READING WAS FALSE IN A LIVE WINDOWED APP. `AppShell::new_events` opens a delivery on EVERY winit iteration, so the counter advanced on nothing but time and the difference an agent measured was "my burst, plus however many idle iterations happened while I waited". Two demos asserting `scene/input_state` is side-effect-free went red in CI — `r885_input_state` and `r1419_window_focus`, which had asserted exactly that since R885, and were right to: it is a `HandlerKind::Read`, and a read that reports differently on each call is not a state snapshot. ★IT IS R1757'S OWN HEADLINE DEFECT AT THE OTHER END OF THE FRAME. That round found the RPC drain opening a delivery per request, wrote "the instrument would consume what it measures", fixed the drain, and left the event loop doing the identical thing one layer up — the same shape R1361.1 left when it split the ACQUIRE block out of `render_us` and kept the PRESENT block in. Fixing one end of a symmetry is not fixing the symmetry, and both times the unfixed end was the one nobody had a test standing on. THE REPAIR: `open_key_delivery` marks a delivery PENDING with its instant and `take_key_delivery` consumes the id, called by the first keystroke of that delivery, so an iteration carrying no keystroke burns no number and `opened` counts deliveries THAT DELIVERED — the only kind an agent can observe. R1658's ordering guarantee is untouched because the instant is still stamped before any handler runs; only the numbering waits. ★THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT REPAIR WAS A FOOT-GUN AND R1658's TESTS FOUND IT: `open_key_delivery` initially returned the arrival a keystroke WOULD carry, so two opens with no keystroke between them previewed the same unclaimed number, and a caller passing that preview to `apply_key_press` — which takes an arrival as an argument and cannot know it was speculative — dispatched two separate deliveries claiming to have arrived together. Three R1658 tests went red. A number nobody has claimed does not exist, so there is nothing honest to return and it returns unit. That is an old gate catching a new mistake for the FOURTH round running (R1747, R1757, R1758, R1760). ★★THE MISSING GATE WAS A DEMO, and that is the round's real lesson: R1757's verification was unit tests and `ShellCore` fixtures, all in-process, and the defect lived in the winit event loop which no in-process test enters, so every local gate passed. `tools/demos/r1760_a_burst_is_one_delivery.py` is what was missing — end-to-end over the wire against a live GUI binding, proving the axis does not move on a half-second wait, that a burst of three advances it by exactly one, that three separate requests advance it by three, that a keyless request moves it not at all, and that the characters actually reached the field. Counterfactuals 2/2 CAUGHT at the demo level, one of them restoring R1757's behaviour exactly. TWO OTHER GATES CLOSED, both from the "what did I leave advisory" list: `commit-msg` refuses a round token an existing commit already carries (the first moment a duplicate is knowable from git — R1759's `worktree.sh` claim covers the window before any commit, and continuations pass by construction since `R1753.1` is a different token from `R1753`, which matters because 106 commits here are `.N` follow-ups), and `land` now prints the exact `git rm` / `git mv` / pin-bump line for what it refuses, since refusing without saying what to do next was half the cost the tool exists to remove. ★SHELLCHECK FOUND A THIRD INSTANCE OF A DEFECT THIS ROUND HAD ALREADY MET TWICE: `tools/test_hooks.sh` carried a backtick inside a double-quoted assertion label, so the suite RAN `git commit` on every invocation — including inside `pre-push`, where it runs — exiting non-zero into a swallowed stream so nothing ever showed it. R1759 hit the same class an hour earlier in `worktree.sh`, found by RUNNING the command rather than by its selftest, and the self-grep that followed covered only that file. VERIFIED: 6,703 tests across five crates, workspace clippy, `test_hooks.sh` 141/0 (129 before), `worktree.sh --selftest`, shellcheck clean on every file touched, harness selftest 118/118, and all TEN demos that read `scene/input_state` passing on Xvfb :97 — the blast radius measured rather than guessed (10 read the axis, 2 assert idempotence, and those 2 are exactly the ones that were red). a page the host paints itself answers for itself, and the route recorded for it was measurably the wrong one. Declared `none`: a section made answerable plus three marks given addresses, no new widget, no new gesture and no axis re-judged against measured evidence. THE PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, NOT ONLY EXPENSIVE. `SectionStanding::Inline` and `docs/analyzer-sections-spec.json` both said closing an inline section means giving that page a `Screen`, and the entry sat twenty-three rounds under a cost estimate. Measured over the wire before writing anything: the page region a screen is granted is 1096x802 at (52, 98), while that section's layout bar is 1096x46 at (52, 52) and its palette 292x848 at (1148, 52) -- a host paints a section's chrome BESIDE the region because that is what chrome is, and a screen judges what it paints, so the recorded route would have shipped a verdict blind to 298,032 px2 of its own section including the surface the reference makes its whole argument with. THE DECISION IS THAT A SCREEN AND A VERDICT ARE TWO AXES: `SectionJudge` answers one question and grants no paint, no hit test, no keys and no accessibility tree; `ScreenRoster::judging` refuses four pairings, of which `a key that already has a screen` is the new one -- two things answering for one section would make the verdict depend on registration order. `Showing` is handed in by the roster from the `Journey` rather than derived by the judge, because a host's inline page has no store of its own to be empty and `away because I found none of my parts` is the escape hatch R1742 refused one level down. WRITING THE PIN FOUND FOUR THINGS: three marks a reader sees and nothing could name (the placed count, the palette's title and its hint, all loose ink), and one reproduction gap -- the reference writes which release fills each palette group into the group's own heading and this build had dropped it, now derived from the tier so the two cannot come apart. TWO OLD GATES CAUGHT THE FIRST DRAFT (a backward census refused the undeclared tag, the voice census refused three undecided regions) and a third, `r1738`'s `a tag exactly when judged`, turned out to be a true statement about a world where only screens could be judged. ZERO-FLAKE: two demos each failed once in the 34-demo blast and passed 20 of 20 isolated re-runs; root-caused as a read racing the render (a paint verdict is about the last frame and `tick` moves the clock, not the frame), repaired in the harness with `frame_count`/`await_paint`/`intervene_painted` and applied at every navigate-then-read-a-verdict site in five demos, with the class censused (12 demos read a verdict; the other three read at boot, where `boot_grace` covers it).
